This%0A * layer creates the overlay first, then the app code runs against it.%0A *%0A * Why a shadow root: a bookmarklet runs inside the host page and the page's own%0A * CSS would shred the app's layout. A shadow root isolates both directions, and%0A * a **constructed stylesheet** (`new CSSStyleSheet()` + adoptedStyleSheets)%0A * sidesteps `style-src`, which blocks an injected `<style>` on a strict-CSP page.%0A *%0A * Nothing here becomes a global on the host page: the vendored libraries are%0A * evaluated against a shadow object (`Object.create(window)`), so a page already%0A * shipping its own SheetJS or PapaParse keeps its own copies.%0A * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */%0A%0Avar TS_BMK = __TS_BMK__;                       // { variant, libs, css, markup, … } injected by build.js%0Avar TS_HOST_ID = 'turnstone-bookmarklet-root';%0A%0Avar ROOT = null;                               // the app's element root — all its queries scope here%0Avar THEME_ROOT = null;                         // element carrying data-theme%0Avar TS_HOST = null, TS_SHADOW = null, TS_APP = null;%0A%0Aif (document.getElementById(TS_HOST_ID)) {%0A  throw new Error('Turnstone is already running on this page — close it first (✕ in the top bar).');%0A}%0A%0A/* --- Host shell: a 26px bar (carry state / close) + the app viewport ------- */%0ATS_HOST = document.createElement('div');%0ATS_HOST.id = TS_HOST_ID;%0ATS_HOST.setAttribute('data-turnstone-variant', TS_BMK.variant);%0ATS_HOST.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:0;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;z-index:2147483647;margin:0;padding:0;' +%0A  'background:%230f1115;color:%23e6e9ef;font:13px/1.45 system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif;' +%0A  'display:flex;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden';%0Adocument.documentElement.appendChild(TS_HOST);%0A%0ATS_SHADOW = TS_HOST.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });%0ATS_SHADOW.innerHTML =%0A  '<div id="ts-bar">' +%0A    '<span class="ts-brand">Turnstone</span>' +%0A    '<span class="ts-variant"></span>' +%0A    '<span class="ts-spacer"></span>' +%0A    '<button type="button" id="ts-copy" title="Copy this queue as JSON — paste it back later with Restore">Copy state</button>' +%0A    '<button type="button" id="ts-restore" title="Paste a state JSON copied earlier and keep going">Restore state</button>' +%0A    '<button type="button" id="ts-close" title="Close Turnstone and return to the page">✕ Close</button>' +%0A  '</div>' +%0A  '<div id="ts-app">' + TS_BMK.markup + '</div>';%0A%0AROOT = TS_SHADOW.getElementById('ts-app');%0ATS_APP = ROOT;%0ATHEME_ROOT = TS_HOST;%0A%0A/* Styles that go into the shadow root: constructed sheet when available (CSP-proof),%0A   a plain <style> otherwise. Used for both the bar and the app's own stylesheet. */%0Afunction tsAdoptCss(text) {%0A  try {%0A    if (typeof CSSStyleSheet === 'function' && 'adoptedStyleSheets' in ShadowRoot.prototype) {%0A      var sheet = new CSSStyleSheet();%0A      sheet.replaceSync(text);%0A      TS_SHADOW.adoptedStyleSheets = TS_SHADOW.adoptedStyleSheets.concat(sheet);%0A      return 'constructed';%0A    }%0A  } catch (e) { console.warn('[Turnstone] constructed stylesheet unavailable', e); IndexedDB is shadowed with an in-memory stand-in so%0A * the app's snapshot code keeps working for the tab's lifetime — and the user's%0A * queue is never written into the host site's database. localStorage stays real%0A * (every access in the app is already guarded) because that is what remembers%0A * theme, open mode and column presets: small, namespaced keys. */%0Avar indexedDB = (function memIndexedDb() {%0A  var stores = {};%0A  function request() { return { result: undefined, onsuccess: null, onerror: null }; }%0A  function soon(fn) { setTimeout(fn, 0); }%0A  function makeStore(name) {%0A    if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(stores, name)) stores[name] = new Map();%0A    var map = stores[name];%0A    return {%0A      put: function (value) {%0A        var req = request();%0A        soon(function () { map.set(value.key, value); req.result = value.key; if (req.onsuccess) req.onsuccess(); });%0A        return req;%0A      },%0A      get: function (key) {%0A        var req = request();%0A        soon(function () { req.result = map.get(key); if (req.onsuccess) req.onsuccess(); });%0A        return req;%0A      },%0A      getAll: function () {%0A        var req = request();%0A        soon(function () { req.result = Array.from(map.values()); if (req.onsuccess) req.onsuccess(); });%0A        return req;%0A      },%0A      delete: function (key) {%0A        var req = request();%0A        soon(function () { map.delete(key); if (req.onsuccess) req.onsuccess(); });%0A        return req;%0A      },%0A      clear: function () {%0A        var req = request();%0A        soon(function () { map.clear(); if (req.onsuccess) req.onsuccess(); });%0A        return req;%0A      },%0A    };%0A  }%0A  return {%0A    open: function (name) {%0A      var req = request();%0A      soon(function () {%0A        req.result = {%0A          name: name,%0A          objectStoreNames: { contains: function (n) { return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(stores, n); } },%0A          createObjectStore: function (n) { makeStore(n); return {}; },%0A          transaction: function (n) {%0A            var os = makeStore(n);%0A            var tx = { objectStore: function () { return os; }, oncomplete: null, onerror: null, error: null };%0A            soon(function () { if (tx.oncomplete) tx.oncomplete(); });   // writes above are queued first%0A            return tx;%0A          },%0A        };%0A        if (req.onupgradeneeded) req.onupgradeneeded();%0A        if (req.onsuccess) req.onsuccess();%0A      });%0A      return req;%0A    },%0A  };%0A})();%0A%0A/* PapaParse stand-in — the app's API surface, in ~2 KB, no dependency. */%0A/* PapaParse stand-in — the exact slice of the API app.html consumes.%0A *%0A *   Papa.parse(text, { skipEmptyLines: 'greedy', delimiter }) -> { data, errors, meta: { delimiter } }%0A *   Papa.unparse(matrix, { delimiter })                        -> string%0A *%0A * Real RFC-4180 behaviour (quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded commas and%0A * newlines, CRLF, BOM) plus delimiter sniffing, in ~2 KB and with no dependency.%0A * That is what lets the zero-library bookmarklet keep full CSV/TSV support —%0A * the hosted app loads the real PapaParse through vendor/ instead.%0A */%0Avar Papa = (function () {%0A  var CANDIDATES = [',', '\t', ';', '|'];%0A%0A  /** Delimiter counts on a line, ignoring anything inside quotes. */%0A  function countOutsideQuotes(line, delim) {%0A    var n = 0, quoted = false;%0A    for (var i = 0; i < line.length; i++) {%0A      var ch = line[i];%0A      if (quoted) {%0A        if (ch === '"') {%0A          if (line[i + 1] === '"') i++;%0A          else quoted = false;%0A        }%0A      } else if (ch === '"') quoted = true;%0A      else if (ch === delim) n++;%0A    }%0A    return n;%0A  }%0A%0A  /** Pick the delimiter that splits the most lines into the same number of fields. */%0A  function sniff(text) {%0A    var lines = text.split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, 30).filter(function (l) { return l.trim() !== ''; });%0A    if (!lines.length) return ',';%0A    var best = ',', bestScore = 0;%0A    for (var c = 0; c < CANDIDATES.length; c++) {%0A      var d = CANDIDATES[c];%0A      var counts = lines.map(function (l) { return countOutsideQuotes(l, d); });%0A      var sorted = counts.slice().sort(function (a, b) { return a - b; });%0A      var median = sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)];%0A      if (median < 1) continue;                                     // delim never appears%0A      var agree = counts.filter(function (n) { return n === median; }).length / counts.length;%0A      var score = median * agree;%0A      if (score > bestScore) { bestScore = score; best = d; }%0A    }%0A    return best;%0A  }%0A%0A  /** RFC-4180 state machine. Unterminated quotes are an error, not a crash. */%0A  function splitRows(text, delim, errors) {%0A    var rows = [], row = [], field = '', quoted = false, i = 0;%0A    var sawField = false;%0A    while (i < text.length) {%0A      var ch = text[i];%0A      if (quoted) {%0A        if (ch === '"') {%0A          if (text[i + 1] === '"') { field += '"'; i += 2; continue; }%0A          quoted = false; i++; continue;%0A        }%0A        field += ch; i++; continue;%0A      }%0A      if (ch === '"' && field === '') { quoted = true; sawField = true; i++; continue; }%0A      if (ch === delim) { row.push(field); field = ''; sawField = true; i++; continue; }%0A      if (ch === '\r') { i++; continue; }                            // CRLF or lone CR%0A      if (ch === '\n') {%0A        if (field !== '' || sawField || row.length) { row.push(field); rows.push(row); }%0A        row = []; field = ''; sawField = false; i++; continue;%0A      }%0A      field += ch; sawField = true; i++;%0A    }%0A    if (quoted) errors.push({ type: 'Quotes', message: 'Unterminated quoted field', row: rows.length });%0A    if (field !== '' || sawField || row.length) { row.push(field); rows.push(row); }%0A    return rows;%0A  }%0A%0A  function parse(text, opts) {%0A    opts = opts || {};%0A    var errors = [];%0A    var delim = opts.delimiter || sniff(text);%0A    var data = splitRows(String(text == null ? '' : text), delim, errors);%0A    if (opts.skipEmptyLines) {%0A      data = data.filter(function (r) { return r.some(function (c) { return String(c).trim() !== ''; }); });%0A    }%0A    return { data: data, errors: errors, meta: { delimiter: delim } };%0A  }%0A%0A  function needsQuotes(s, delim) {%0A    return s.indexOf('"') >= 0 || s.indexOf('\n') >= 0 || s.indexOf('\r') >= 0%0A      || s.indexOf(delim) >= 0 || s.charAt(0) === ' ' || s.charAt(s.length - 1) === ' ';%0A  }%0A%0A  function unparse(rows, opts) {%0A    var delim = (opts && opts.delimiter) || ',';%0A    return rows.map(function (row) {%0A      return row.map(function (cell) {%0A        var s = cell == null ? '' : String(cell);%0A        return needsQuotes(s, delim) ? '"' + s.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"' : s;%0A      }).join(delim);%0A    }).join('\n');%0A  }%0A%0A  return {%0A    parse: parse,%0A    unparse: unparse,%0A    shim: true,                       // app/payload can log which implementation is live%0A  };%0A})();%0A%0A%0A(function(){%0A%0A'use strict';%0A/* =========================================================================%0A   Project Turnstone — zero-server URL-list processor.%0A   Vanilla JS. Workspace on the LEFT, task sidebar on the RIGHT (deviation).%0A   ========================================================================= */%0A%0Aconst LOG = '[Turnstone]';%0Aconst log  = (...a) => console.log(LOG, ...a);%0Aconst warn = (...a) => console.warn(LOG, ...a);%0Aconst err  = (...a) => console.error(LOG, ...a);%0A%0A/* ---------------------------- IndexedDB layer ---------------------------- */%0Aconst DB_NAME = 'turnstone', DB_VER = 1;%0Alet idbPromise = null;%0A%0Afunction idbOpen() {%0A  if (idbPromise) return idbPromise;%0A  idbPromise = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {%0A    const req = indexedDB.open(DB_NAME, DB_VER);%0A    req.onupgradeneeded = () => {%0A      const db = req.result;%0A      if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains('handles')) db.createObjectStore('handles', { keyPath: 'key' });%0A      if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains('session')) db.createObjectStore('session', { keyPath: 'key' });%0A      log('IndexedDB stores created');%0A    };%0A    req.onsuccess = () => { log('IndexedDB opened');  return String(s ?? '').replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;', "'": '&%2339;' }[c]));%0A}%0Afunction highlight(text, q) {%0A  const raw = String(text ?? '');%0A  if (!q) return esc(raw);%0A  const rx = new RegExp(q.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'), 'gi');%0A  return raw.split(rx).map(esc).join('<mark>' + esc(q) + '</mark>'); // split keeps separators; escape every part%0A}%0Afunction escapeRegExp(s) { return s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'); }%0A%0Alet toastTimer = null;%0Afunction toast(msg, type = '') {%0A  log('Toast:', msg);%0A  els.toast.textContent = msg;%0A  els.toast.className = 'show ' + type;%0A  clearTimeout(toastTimer);%0A  toastTimer = setTimeout(() => { els.toast.className = ''; }, 3500);%0A}%0A%0Aasync function copyText(text, label = 'text') {%0A  try {%0A    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);%0A    log(`Copied ${label} to clipboard (${text.length} chars)`);%0A    return true;%0A  } catch (e) {%0A    warn('Clipboard API failed, falling back to execCommand', e);%0A    const ta = document.createElement('textarea');%0A    ta.value = text; ta.className = 'clip-fallback';%0A    document.body.appendChild(ta); ta.select();%0A    const ok = document.execCommand('copy');%0A    ta.remove();%0A    log(`execCommand copy ${ok ? 'succeeded' : 'failed'} for ${label}`);%0A    return ok;%0A  }%0A}%0A%0A/* ------------------------------ Parsing core ------------------------------ */%0A/* Every supported input — CSV, TSV, XLSX/XLS/ODS, JSON, HTML tables, XML —%0A   collapses into ONE shape: a 2D array of strings. Everything downstream%0A   (analyzeMatrix → loadMatrix → renderCards) is format-agnostic, so adding a%0A   format means one detector entry plus one parser that returns rows. */%0A%0Aconst HEADER_URL_RE = /^(url|link|href|website|web site|site|address|loc|permalink|portal|record|open in)\b/i;%0A/* The words real trackers use for "the thing this row is about". A vendor%0A   onboarding sheet, a ticket queue, an approvals list and a candidate pipeline%0A   all name this column something other than "Name" — and the column that *does*%0A   read like a label on those sheets is the identifier beside it. */%0Aconst HEADER_NAME_RE = /^(name|title|task|label|page|description|summary|subject|item|issue|request|job|candidate|applicant|vendor|supplier|client|customer|company|asset|document|contract|policy|renewal|action|deliverable|activity|step|milestone|what|thing)\b/i;%0A/* Identifier columns: `INC0041821` is what you *find* a row by, never what the%0A   row is. Recognized so a title column can outrank it — ``%232``, not ``%231``. */%0Aconst HEADER_ID_RE = /^(id|no|num|number|ref|reference|code|key|%23|ticket|case|invoice|order|po|sku|uid|guid|index|seq|sequence|row)(\b|$)/i;%0A%0A/* A cell is a URL *value* when it looks like a link, whatever its column is%0A   called. This is the only test used to choose the URL column: the header text%0A   is at most a tiebreaker, so a list whose URL column is titled "Page",%0A   "Resource" or nothing at all still lands on the right column. */%0Aconst URL_VALUE_RE = /^https?:\/\//i;%0Aconst DOMAIN_VALUE_RE = /^(?:www\.)?([a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)*\.[a-z]{2,})(?:[/?%23].*)?$/i;%0Aconst FILE_EXT_TLDS = new Set(['exe','txt','doc','docx','pdf','zip','png','jpg','jpeg','gif','csv','tsv','xls','xlsx','ods','json','html','htm','xml','md','log','bak','tmp','py','js','ts','css','mp3','mp4','svg','ppt','pptx','tar','gz','rar','7z','iso','dmg','apk']);%0A/* A label, not a value: short, readable, and free of the marks that give a real%0A   data value away — a long digit run (`INC0041821`), a date, an address, a link,%0A   or a number pretending to be a word. "Phone 1" and "Q3 notes" are labels;%0A   "1200" and "2024-05-12" are not. */%0Aconst LABEL_SHAPE_RE = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9 ._/%23&'()%25+\-]{0,39}$/;%0Afunction looksLikeLabel(v) {%0A  const s = String(v ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!s) return false;%0A  if (/\d{3,}/.test(s)) return false;%0A  if (DATE_SHAPE_RE.test(s)) return false;%0A  return LABEL_SHAPE_RE.test(s) && !isUrlValue(s) && !isEmailValue(s) && !isPhoneValue(s);%0A}%0A/** Is `first` a header row over `sample`? Every filled cell must read as a label%0A    and at least one column must hold values that are *not* labels below it —%0A    otherwise a two-row list of plain names would be promoted to a header. */%0Afunction looksLikeLabelRow(first, sample) {%0A  const cells = first.map(c => String(c ?? '').trim());%0A  const filled = cells.filter(Boolean);%0A  if (filled.length < 2) return false;%0A  if (!filled.every(looksLikeLabel)) return false;%0A  for (let c = 0; c < cells.length; c++) {%0A    let values = 0, nonLabels = 0;%0A    for (const r of sample) {%0A      const v = String(r[c] ?? '').trim();%0A      if (!v) continue;%0A      values++;%0A      if (!looksLikeLabel(v)) nonLabels++;%0A    }%0A    if (values >= 2 && nonLabels / values >= 0.6) return true;%0A  }%0A  return false;%0A}%0Afunction isUrlValue(v) {%0A  const s = String(v ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!s) return false;%0A  if (URL_VALUE_RE.test(s)) return true;%0A  const m = s.match(DOMAIN_VALUE_RE);%0A  if (!m) return false;%0A  const tld = m[1].slice(m[1].lastIndexOf('.') + 1).toLowerCase();%0A  return !FILE_EXT_TLDS.has(tld);   // "setup.exe" is a filename, not a link%0A}%0A%0A/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *%0A   Portal lists: work that lives behind one URL%0A   ------------------------------------------------------------------ *%0A   A large share of real admin queues carries no link at all. The rows are%0A   ticket numbers, invoice IDs, vendor names or case references, the portal is%0A   the same page every time, and the *key* to a row is a column value — not an%0A   address. Turnstone's link detection is value-based and rightly finds nothing%0A   there, so the list gets a template instead: the user names the portal once%0A   (or arrives with `?link=`) and every row composes its own URL.%0A%0A   `{Column name}` is filled from that column and percent-encoded, because that%0A   is what a path segment or a query value needs 90%25 of the time. `{Column|raw}`%0A   splices the value verbatim for the other 10%25 — a template that rebuilds a%0A   path the value already spells out. `{0}` addresses a column by index, so a%0A   file with no header row can still be templated. */%0Aconst TEMPLATE_FIELD_RE = /\{([^{}]+)\}/g;%0Aconst isHttpUrl = (s) => /^https?:\/\//i.test(String(s ?? '').trim());%0A%0A/** The distinct placeholders a template names, `|raw` stripped (for the UI). */%0Afunction templateFields(tpl) {%0A  const out = [];%0A  TEMPLATE_FIELD_RE.lastIndex = 0;%0A  let m;%0A  while ((m = TEMPLATE_FIELD_RE.exec(String(tpl ?? '')))) {%0A    const name = m[1].trim().replace(/\|raw$/i, '').trim();%0A    if (name && !out.includes(name)) out.push(name);%0A  }%0A  return out;%0A}%0A%0A/** Resolve one placeholder against a row: header name (case-insensitive) first,%0A    then a bare column index. Returns null when nothing matches, '' when the%0A    column exists but this row is empty — the difference decides the warning. */%0Afunction resolveTemplateField(field, row, header) {%0A  const name = String(field).trim();%0A  const idx = header.findIndex(h => String(h ?? '').trim().toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase());%0A  if (idx >= 0) return String(row[idx] ?? '').trim();%0A  if (/^\d+$/.test(name) && Number(name) < row.length) return String(row[Number(name)] ?? '').trim();%0A  return null;%0A}%0A%0A/** Compose one row's URL. `''` means "this row has no link" — either the template%0A    is blank, a placeholder has no matching column, or the row's key is empty.%0A    A missing *column* is a template mistake and is reported once; a blank *cell*%0A    is simply a row without a key, which is ordinary and stays quiet. */%0Afunction applyUrlTemplate(tpl, row, header) {%0A  let t = String(tpl ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!t) return '';%0A  // A template typed as a bare host means https, the same way it does in the%0A  // address bar. This is the single place that forgives that, so the preview in%0A  // the UI and the URL on a card can never disagree.%0A  if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.\-]*:/i.test(t)) t = 'https://' + t;%0A  /* An empty value is fatal in the *path* and harmless in the query. A portal%0A     address like `/incident/` with the ticket number missing is not a link to%0A     this row, it is a link to the wrong page — so there is no link. `?tag=` with%0A     an empty tag is just an empty filter, and dropping the whole row's link over%0A     it would be worse than keeping it. */%0A  const queryAt = t.search(/[?%23]/);%0A  let missing = false;%0A  const url = t.replace(TEMPLATE_FIELD_RE, (whole, field, offset) => {%0A    const name = field.trim().replace(/\|raw$/i, '').trim();%0A    const raw = /\|raw$/i.test(field.trim());%0A    const value = resolveTemplateField(name, row, header);%0A    if (value === null) { missing = true; return ''; }%0A    if (value === '' && (queryAt < 0 || offset < queryAt)) { missing = true; return ''; }%0A    return raw ? value : encodeURIComponent(value);%0A  }).trim();%0A  if (missing) return '';%0A  /* Last gate before a value becomes a clickable href: only a real http(s) URL%0A     comes back, so no template can ever produce a `javascript:` or `data:` link. */%0A  return isHttpUrl(url) ? url : '';%0A}%0A%0A/** The host a template points at — used to label a constant portal URL. */%0Afunction portalLabel(tpl) {%0A  try { return new URL(String(tpl).replace(/\{[^{}]*\}/g, 'x')).host || 'the portal'; }%0A  catch (e) { return 'the portal'; }%0A}%0A%0A/** Validate a template against the loaded columns. Returns a human reason, or null. */%0Afunction templateProblem(tpl, header) {%0A  const t = String(tpl ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!t) return null;%0A  if (/^\s*(javascript|data|vbscript|file|blob):/i.test(t)) return 'Only http:// and https:// templates are allowed';%0A  const names = header.map(h => String(h ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());%0A  const unknown = templateFields(t).filter(f => !names.includes(f.toLowerCase()) && !/^\d+$/.test(f));%0A  if (unknown.length) {%0A    const cols = header.filter(h => String(h ?? '').trim()).map(h => `“${String(h).trim()}”`).join(', ');%0A    return `No column called ${unknown.map(u => `“${u}”`).join(' or ')} — ${cols ? `this file has ${cols}` : 'this file has no header row, so use {0}, {1} … by position'}`;%0A  }%0A  return null;%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Remembered portal templates ---------------------------------------- */%0A/* Keyed by header signature, exactly like column roles and presets, so the same%0A   report opened next month composes its links again without being asked. A file%0A   with no header row has no signature to key on, so its template is not%0A   remembered — it is re-entered (or passed with `?link=`) each time. */%0Aconst LS_TEMPLATES = 'turnstone-link-templates';%0Afunction loadTemplates() {%0A  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_TEMPLATES) || '{}'); }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not read saved link templates', e); return {}; }%0A}%0Afunction saveTemplates(t) {%0A  try { localStorage.setItem(LS_TEMPLATES, JSON.stringify(t)); return true; }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not persist link template', e); return false; }%0A}%0A/** A header signature is only meaningful when there is a header row. */%0Aconst templateKeyFor = (data, hasHeader) => (hasHeader ? headerSignature((data || [])[0] || []) : '');%0Afunction rememberTemplate(key, tpl) {%0A  if (!key) return;%0A  const all = loadTemplates();%0A  if (String(tpl || '').trim()) all[key] = String(tpl).trim();%0A  else delete all[key];%0A  if (saveTemplates(all)) log(`Link template ${tpl ? 'saved' : 'cleared'} for this header signature`);%0A}%0A%0A/* An address and a phone number are the other two "link-shaped" values a list%0A   can carry, and they are decided from the *value* for the same reason a URL is:%0A   nobody's CRM export calls those columns what we would. Turnstone vendors the%0A   two embedded layers that make the click useful — MailLayer for addresses,%0A   PhoneLayer for numbers — so a click opens a webmail composer or a VoIP/SMS%0A   provider picker instead of a dead desktop handler. */%0Aconst EMAIL_VALUE_RE = /^[a-z0-9._%25+'\-]+@[a-z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9\-]+)+$/i;%0Aconst PHONE_VALUE_RE = /^\+?\d[\d\s().\u2011\u2013\-/]{4,}\d$/;%0Aconst DATE_SHAPE_RE = /^\d{4}[-/.]\d{1,2}[-/.]\d{1,2}$/;   // 2024-05-12 is a date, not a number%0Afunction isEmailValue(v) {%0A  const s = String(v ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!s || s.length > 254 || /\s/.test(s)) return false;%0A  if (!EMAIL_VALUE_RE.test(s)) return false;%0A  const tld = s.slice(s.lastIndexOf('.') + 1);%0A  return tld.length >= 2 && !/\d/.test(tld);   // "a@b.12" is not an address%0A}%0A/* Money and measurements are not telephone numbers. `12480.75` is an invoice%0A   amount with seven digits in it, and it read as a phone number — which was%0A   enough, on its own, to stop a finance sheet being recognized as a list whose%0A   rows are worked in one portal. A decimal number has one dot (or a thousands%0A   separator) and a fraction; a dotted phone number (555.123.4567) has two or%0A   three groups instead. */%0Aconst DECIMAL_NUMBER_RE = /^-?(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+)(?:\.\d+)?$|^-?\d+\.\d+$/;%0Afunction isPhoneValue(v) {%0A  const s = String(v ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!s || DATE_SHAPE_RE.test(s) || DECIMAL_NUMBER_RE.test(s)) return false;%0A  if (!PHONE_VALUE_RE.test(s)) return false;%0A  const digits = s.replace(/\D/g, '');%0A  return digits.length >= 7 && digits.length <= 15;   // E.164 stops at 15 digits%0A}%0A/** Which kind of link a cell value is — the one place that decides href shape. */%0Afunction linkKindOf(v) {%0A  const s = String(v ?? '').trim();%0A  if (!s) return null;%0A  if (isUrlValue(s)) return 'url';%0A  if (isEmailValue(s)) return 'email';%0A  if (isPhoneValue(s)) return 'phone';%0A  return null;%0A}%0A/** Where a link-shaped value should actually go. */%0Afunction linkHrefOf(v) {%0A  const s = String(v ?? '').trim();%0A  const kind = linkKindOf(s);%0A  if (kind === 'email') return `mailto:${s}`;%0A  if (kind === 'phone') return `tel:${s.replace(/(?!^\+)[^\d]/g, '')}`;   // same sanitization PhoneLayer applies%0A  return s;%0A}%0A/* A link column usually wants a page over an address over a bare number, so a list%0A   with both a Website and an Email column still leads with the website. */%0Aconst LINK_WEIGHT = { url: 2, email: 1.5, phone: 1 };%0Aconst LAYER_ACCENT = { dark: '%237aa2ff', light: '%233b66d0' };%0Aconst currentTheme = () => (THEME_ROOT.dataset.theme === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark');%0A/** PhoneLayer documents per-trigger colour/theme overrides — stamp them, so its%0A    provider picker matches the app instead of arriving in its own light default. */%0Aconst layerAnchorAttrs = (kind) => kind === 'phone'%0A  ? ` data-phonelayer-color="${LAYER_ACCENT[currentTheme()]}" data-phonelayer-theme="${currentTheme()}"`%0A  : '';%0A%0A/* Completed/status + notes columns. We emit "Status"/"Notes" on export, but a%0A   file dropped back in (or built elsewhere) may label them Completed / Done /%0A   Finished / Checked / Comment — accepting that whole family is what lets a%0A   re-import resume the user's progress instead of resetting every card. */%0A/* Pipeline vocabulary included on purpose: a vendor tracker says Stage, a%0A   candidate pipeline says Stage or Phase, a project sheet says Progress. Those%0A   are the same column as Status, and a list whose status column goes unrecognized%0A   loses every tick the user made in the system it came from. */%0Aconst HEADER_STATUS_RE = /^(status|state|stage|phase|progress|complet(e|ed|ion)|done|finished|checked|reviewed|processed|handled|result|outcome|disposition)\b/i;%0Aconst HEADER_NOTES_RE  = /^(notes?|comments?|remarks?|memo)\b/i;%0Aconst STATUS_HEADER_WORDS = new Set(['status', 'state', 'stage', 'phase', 'progress', 'complete', 'completed', 'completion', 'done', 'finished', 'checked', 'reviewed', 'processed', 'handled', 'result', 'outcome', 'disposition']);%0Aconst NOTES_HEADER_WORDS  = new Set(['note', 'notes', 'comment', 'comments', 'remark', 'remarks', 'memo']);%0Aconst normalizeHeader = (h) => String(h ?? '').toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z]/g, '');%0A%0A/** Cell values that mean "this task is done". Ticks are accepted so rows pasted%0A    from a spreadsheet round-trip, and a completion *date* counts as done too. */%0A/* Terminal states, as the systems these lists come out of spell them. Turnstone%0A   asks "has this row been handled?", not "did it succeed?" — so a closed ticket,%0A   a paid invoice and a rejected application are all done with, because the queue%0A   is what matters. Every in-flight word (open, new, pending, awaiting, in%0A   progress, blocked) is deliberately absent, and the two tests below are anchored%0A   to the whole value, so "Pending approval" can never read as "Approved". */%0Aconst COMPLETE_RE = /^(complete|completed|done|finished|yes|y|true|1|x|✓|✔|☑|✅|closed?|resolved|approved?|accepted|paid|sent|signed|shipped|filed|submitted|handled|processed|cancell?ed|declined|rejected|void|archived|reconciled|verified|published|renewed|delivered|no action needed)$/i;%0Aconst COMPLETE_DATE_RE = /^\d{4}-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}([T ].*)?$/;%0A/* Same test after stripping decoration, so "✓ done", "done ✓" and "- complete"%0A   all count. Anchored matches keep "not done" and "incomplete" safely false. */%0Aconst DONE_DECOR_RE = /[\s✓✔☑✅·•\-–—:]/g;%0Aconst isCompleteValue = (raw) => {%0A  const v = String(raw ?? '').trim().replace(/\uFE0F/g, '');   // drop emoji variation selectors%0A  if (!v) return false;%0A  return COMPLETE_RE.test(v) || COMPLETE_RE.test(v.replace(DONE_DECOR_RE, '')) || COMPLETE_DATE_RE.test(v);%0A};%0A%0A/* `writable` = we can rebuild the file byte-for-byte in its own format, so edits%0A   save silently in place. Everything else is a one-way import: its edits live in%0A   browser storage until the user exports CSV/XLSX. XLS/XLSM/XLSB/ODS are read-only%0A   on purpose — writing XLSX bytes under a .xls/.xlsm name would drop macros and%0A   mislabel the file. */%0Aconst FORMAT_INFO = {%0A  csv:  { label: 'CSV',        writable: true  },%0A  tsv:  { label: 'TSV',        writable: true  },%0A  xlsx: { label: 'XLSX',       writable: true  },%0A  xls:  { label: 'XLS',        writable: false },%0A  xlsm: { label: 'XLSM',       writable: false },%0A  xlsb: { label: 'XLSB',       writable: false },%0A  ods:  { label: 'ODS',        writable: false },%0A  docx: { label: 'Word doc',   writable: false },%0A  md:   { label: 'Markdown',   writable: false },%0A  doc:  { label: 'Word 97-2003', writable: false },%0A  json: { label: 'JSON',       writable: false },%0A  html: { label: 'HTML table', writable: false },%0A  xml:  { label: 'XML',        writable: false },%0A  eml:  { label: 'Email (.eml)', writable: false },%0A  pdf:  { label: 'PDF',        writable: false },%0A};%0A/** The formats welcome-panel / drop-zone copy advertises. One place, so the%0A    advertised list and the accepted list cannot drift apart. */%0Aconst ADVERTISED_FORMATS = ['CSV · TSV', 'XLSX / XLS / ODS', 'DOCX', 'Email (.eml)', 'Markdown', 'JSON · HTML · XML'];%0Aconst formatLabel = (f) => (FORMAT_INFO[f] || {}).label || String(f || '').toUpperCase();%0A/** Formats whose matrix can be written back into the source file in place. */%0Aconst isWritable = (f) => !!(FORMAT_INFO[f] && FORMAT_INFO[f].writable);%0A%0A/* Workbook support is a **capability**, not a build assumption. The bookmarklet's%0A   no-library variant and the standalone CSV-only build ship without SheetJS, and%0A   the app must degrade out loud: refuse `.xlsx` with a real reason, hide the XLSX%0A   export, and say so on the welcome panel — never fail on the first workbook. */%0Aconst HAS_XLSX = typeof XLSX === 'object' && XLSX !== null && typeof XLSX.read === 'function';%0A/* Reading a workbook and *rebuilding* one are separate capabilities: a build can%0A   ship a read-only workbook reader (the bookmarklet's zero-library variant does)%0A   and must then treat workbooks as one-way imports instead of promising a%0A   write-back it cannot deliver. */%0Aconst HAS_XLSX_WRITE = HAS_XLSX && typeof XLSX.write === 'function';%0A/* The two embedded layers are a capability like any other. MailLayer publishes no%0A   global, so the pair is read from PhoneLayer's: they are vendored together and a%0A   build has both or neither. Without them an address still opens the system mail%0A   handler and a number the system dialler — so the app degrades, it never breaks. */%0Aconst HAS_LAYERS = typeof window.PhoneLayer === 'object' && window.PhoneLayer !== null;%0A/* Some builds have no durable storage at all — the bookmarklet overlay runs on a%0A   throwaway origin and shadows IndexedDB. Those builds must say so instead of%0A   promising a snapshot that will not outlive the tab. */%0Aconst SESSION_ONLY = true;   // ports/bookmarklet/build.js flips this to true%0Aconst storageLabel = () => (SESSION_ONLY ? 'this tab only' : 'browser storage');%0A/** Formats we can rebuild in place, given this build's capabilities. */%0Aconst canWrite = (f) => isWritable(f) && (!isWorkbookFormat(f) || HAS_XLSX_WRITE);%0A/** Everything SheetJS opens as a workbook container. */%0Aconst isWorkbookFormat = (f) => f === 'xlsx' || f === 'xls' || f === 'xlsm' || f === 'xlsb' || f === 'ods';%0A%0A/* Extension → format. Explicit aliases only; content sniffing outranks them. */%0Aconst EXT_FORMAT = {%0A  csv: 'csv', txt: 'csv', tsv: 'tsv', tab: 'tsv',%0A  xlsx: 'xlsx', xlsm: 'xlsm', xlsb: 'xlsb', xls: 'xls', ods: 'ods',%0A  json: 'json', jsonl: 'json', ndjson: 'json',%0A  html: 'html', htm: 'html', xml: 'xml', rss: 'xml', atom: 'xml', opml: 'xml',%0A  /* .mht / .mhtml are the same MIME container as .eml — a saved page is a%0A     multipart message whose body part is HTML — so one parser reads both. */%0A  eml: 'eml', mht: 'eml', mhtml: 'eml',%0A  pdf: 'pdf', docx: 'docx',%0A  md: 'md', markdown: 'md', mdown: 'md', mkd: 'md',%0A};%0Aconst CT_FORMAT = [%0A  [/spreadsheetml|ms-excel|excel/, 'xlsx'],%0A  [/opendocument\.spreadsheet/, 'ods'],%0A  [/wordprocessingml|msword/, 'docx'],%0A  [/markdown/, 'md'],%0A  [/rfc822|ms-outlook/, 'eml'],%0A  [/json/, 'json'],%0A  [/html/, 'html'],%0A  [/xml/, 'xml'],%0A  [/tab-separated/, 'tsv'],%0A  [/csv|comma-separated/, 'csv'],%0A  [/pdf/, 'pdf'],%0A];%0A%0Aconst MAGIC = {%0A  pdf: [0x25, 0x50, 0x44, 0x46], // %25PDF%0A  ole: [0xd0, 0xcf, 0x11, 0xe0], // OLE2 container — legacy .xls and .doc%0A  zip: [0x50, 0x4b, 0x03, 0x04], // PK\x03\x04 — xlsx / xlsm / xlsb / ods / docx%0A};%0Afunction hasMagic(buf, bytes) {%0A  return buf.byteLength >= bytes.length && bytes.every((b, i) => new DataView(buf).getUint8(i) === b);%0A}%0A/** An OLE2 file is Word when its stream directory names a WordDocument stream.%0A    The directory stores names as UTF-16LE, so the marker arrives NUL-interleaved. */%0Afunction oleLooksLikeWord(buf) {%0A  const head = new Uint8Array(buf, 0, Math.min(buf.byteLength, 8192));%0A  return new TextDecoder('utf-16le', { fatal: false }).decode(head).includes('WordDocument');%0A}%0A/** ZIP walking, shared by the DOCX parser. A .docx is a ZIP of XML and browsers%0A    expose DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'), so the container opens with no%0A    library at all — the same technique the bookmarklet's SheetJS stand-in uses%0A    for .xlsx. Reading and rebuilding a Word file are different problems: this is%0A    read-only on purpose, so DOCX stays a one-way import. */%0A/* Reading DOCX needs two browser capabilities, and they are worth naming apart:%0A   inflating a ZIP member (`DecompressionStream`) and reading the XML inside it%0A   (`DOMParser`). Every browser with one has the other, but keeping them separate%0A   keeps the capability honest — and lets the container work be tested without a%0A   DOM, which is the only reason `test/run.js` can cover DOCX at all. */%0Aconst HAS_INFLATE = typeof DecompressionStream === 'function';%0Aconst HAS_DOMPARSER = typeof DOMParser === 'function';%0Aconst HAS_ZIP = HAS_INFLATE && HAS_DOMPARSER;%0Aconst ZIP_SIG = { entry: 0x04034b50, cd: 0x02014b50, eocd: 0x06054b50 };%0A/** Central directory as name → { method, compSize, localOffset }. */%0Afunction zipEntries(buf) {%0A  const dv = new DataView(buf);%0A  const floor = Math.max(0, dv.byteLength - 65557 - 22);%0A  let eocd = -1;%0A  for (let i = dv.byteLength - 22; i >= floor; i--) if (dv.getUint32(i, true) === ZIP_SIG.eocd) { eocd = i; break; }%0A  if (eocd < 0) throw new Error('not a ZIP container (no end-of-central-directory record)');%0A  const count = dv.getUint16(eocd + 10, true);%0A  let off = dv.getUint32(eocd + 16, true);%0A  const entries = new Map();%0A  for (let n = 0; n < count; n++) {%0A    if (off + 46 > dv.byteLength || dv.getUint32(off, true) !== ZIP_SIG.cd) break;%0A    const nameLen = dv.getUint16(off + 28, true);%0A    const extraLen = dv.getUint16(off + 30, true);%0A    const commentLen = dv.getUint16(off + 32, true);%0A    entries.set(new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(new Uint8Array(buf, off + 46, nameLen)), {%0A      method: dv.getUint16(off + 10, true),%0A      compSize: dv.getUint32(off + 20, true),%0A      localOffset: dv.getUint32(off + 42, true),%0A    });%0A    off += 46 + nameLen + extraLen + commentLen;%0A  }%0A  return entries;%0A}%0A/** Inflate one member to text. Method 0 (stored) needs no zlib at all. */%0Aasync function zipEntryText(buf, entry) {%0A  const dv = new DataView(buf);%0A  if (dv.getUint32(entry.localOffset, true) !== ZIP_SIG.entry) throw new Error('corrupt ZIP member header');%0A  const start = entry.localOffset + 30 + dv.getUint16(entry.localOffset + 26, true) + dv.getUint16(entry.localOffset + 28, true);%0A  if (entry.method === 0) return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(new Uint8Array(buf, start, entry.compSize));%0A  if (entry.method !== 8) throw new Error(`unsupported ZIP compression method ${entry.method}`);%0A  const stream = new Blob([buf.slice(start, start + entry.compSize)]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'));%0A  return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(await new Response(stream).arrayBuffer());%0A}%0Afunction bufHead(buf, n = 2048) {%0A  return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(buf.slice(0, Math.min(n, buf.byteLength))).replace(/^\uFEFF/, '');%0A}%0A%0A/** Is this text markdown? Only strong, structural signals count: a checklist item,%0A    or a pipe row followed by its `|---|` delimiter. A bulleted list of bare URLs is%0A    deliberately **not** a signal — that stays a one-column .txt list, exactly as it%0A    did before markdown existed, because nothing about it is markdown-specific. */%0Afunction looksLikeMarkdown(text) {%0A  const lines = String(text ?? '').split(/\r?\n/);%0A  let fenced = false;%0A  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {%0A    if (MD_FENCE_RE.test(lines[i])) { fenced = !fenced; continue; }%0A    if (fenced) continue;%0A    if (MD_TASK_RE.test(lines[i])) return true;%0A    if (lines[i].includes('|') && i + 1 < lines.length && mdIsDelimiterRow(lines[i + 1])) return true;%0A  }%0A  return false;%0A}%0A%0A/* An .eml carries no magic bytes and is text, so it has to be recognized by%0A   shape. The test is deliberately strict: an RFC 5322 header block is a run of%0A   `Name: value` fields (plus folded continuations) that ends at the first blank%0A   line, and it has to contain at least two *known* field names. A data row never%0A   survives that — `From,To` has no colon, and a lone `Subject: hi` is one known%0A   field, not two. */%0Aconst RFC822_FIELD_RE = /^([!-9;-~]+):/;%0Aconst RFC822_KNOWN_RE = /^(from|to|cc|bcc|subject|date|received|message-id|in-reply-to|references|mime-version|content-type|content-transfer-encoding|content-disposition|content-id|reply-to|return-path|delivered-to|sender|authentication-results|dkim-signature|x-[a-z0-9-]+)\s*:/i;%0Afunction looksLikeEml(head) {%0A  const lines = String(head || '').split(/\r?\n/);%0A  let known = 0;%0A  const limit = Math.min(lines.length, 80);%0A  for (let i = 0; i < limit; i++) {%0A    const l = lines[i];%0A    if (!l.trim()) {%0A      /* A header block needs something on the other side of the blank line. Two%0A         header-ish lines and then the end of the file is a data row that happens%0A         to contain colons, not a message — and claiming it would turn a two-line%0A         CSV into "this email has no list in it". */%0A      return known >= 2 && lines.slice(i + 1).some(x => x.trim());%0A    }%0A    if (/^[ \t]/.test(l)) continue;        // folded continuation of the field above%0A    if (!RFC822_FIELD_RE.test(l)) return false;%0A    if (RFC822_KNOWN_RE.test(l)) known++;%0A  }%0A  return false;                            // no blank line within 80 lines — not a message%0A}%0A%0A/** Content sniffing for text formats — the strongest signal we have. */%0Afunction sniffTextFormat(head) {%0A  const h = head.trimStart().toLowerCase();%0A  if (!h) return null;%0A  /* Checked before the others: a header block is a far stronger structure than%0A     "starts with [" or "has a pipe row", and a multipart body can contain%0A     anything at all underneath it — including something that looks like a%0A     markdown table. */%0A  if (looksLikeEml(head)) return 'eml';%0A  /* Markdown is checked first because it is the one text format with no magic%0A     bytes *and* no delimiter of its own: a task list or a real pipe table is%0A     unambiguous, and a file that starts with `[` is otherwise claimed by JSON. */%0A  if (looksLikeMarkdown(head)) return 'md';%0A  if (h[0] === '[' || h[0] === '{') return 'json';%0A  if (h.startsWith('<!doctype html') || h.startsWith('<html')) return 'html';%0A  if (h.startsWith('<?xml')) return 'xml';%0A  if (h.startsWith('<!--')) return /<!doctype html|<html|<table/.test(h) ? 'html' : 'xml';    if (h[0] === '<') return /<table\b|<tr\b|<td\b/.test(h) ? 'html' : 'xml';%0A  return null; // delimiter choice is PapaParse's job, not ours%0A}%0A%0A/** Split an extension + Content-Type into soft hints used only when content is inconclusive. */%0Afunction formatHints(name, contentType) {%0A  /* Up to 10 characters, not 5: `.markdown` and `.ndjson` are both longer than the%0A     old cap, so their aliases in EXT_FORMAT were unreachable — the extension simply%0A     failed to match and the file fell through to the delimited-text default. */%0A  const m = String(name || '').match(/\.([a-z0-9]{1,10})(?:$|[?%23])/i);%0A  const ext = m ? m[1].toLowerCase() : null;%0A  const ct = String(contentType || '').toLowerCase();%0A  const hit = CT_FORMAT.find(([re]) => re.test(ct));%0A  return { ext, extFormat: (ext && EXT_FORMAT[ext]) || null, ctFormat: hit ? hit[1] : null, contentType: ct };%0A}%0A%0A/** Decide the format of a buffer. Precedence: magic bytes → content → hints. */%0Afunction detectFormat(buf, name, contentType) {%0A  const hint = formatHints(name, contentType);%0A  let format, why;%0A  if (hasMagic(buf, MAGIC.pdf)) { format = 'pdf'; why = 'magic %25PDF'; }%0A  else if (hasMagic(buf, MAGIC.ole)) {%0A    // The OLE2 container carries both Excel 97-2003 and Word 97-2003; the stream%0A    // directory says which, and only one of them is worth opening.%0A    if (oleLooksLikeWord(buf)) { format = 'doc'; why = 'magic OLE2 (legacy Word)'; }%0A    else { format = 'xls'; why = 'magic OLE2 (legacy Excel)'; }%0A  }%0A  else if (hasMagic(buf, MAGIC.zip)) {%0A    /* xlsx / xlsm / xlsb / ods / docx all share the ZIP magic. The member list%0A       answers it exactly (`word/document.xml` vs `xl/workbook.xml`), so a Word%0A       file renamed to .xlsx still opens as a Word file; the extension is only%0A       the fallback for a container whose directory we cannot walk. */%0A    let zipKind = null;%0A    try {%0A      const names = zipEntries(buf);%0A      if (names.has('word/document.xml')) zipKind = 'docx';%0A      else if (names.has('xl/workbook.xml') || names.has('xl/workbook.bin')) zipKind = isWorkbookFormat(hint.extFormat) ? hint.extFormat : 'xlsx';%0A    } catch (e) { warn('ZIP central directory unreadable — falling back to the file extension', e); }%0A    format = zipKind || (hint.extFormat === 'docx' ? 'docx' : isWorkbookFormat(hint.extFormat) ? hint.extFormat : 'xlsx');%0A    why = `magic PK\\x03\\x04 (ZIP container → ${format})`;%0A  } else {%0A    const sniffed = sniffTextFormat(bufHead(buf));%0A    if (sniffed) { format = sniffed; why = 'content sniff'; }%0A    else if (hint.extFormat) { format = hint.extFormat; why = `extension .${hint.ext}`; }%0A    else if (hint.ctFormat) { format = hint.ctFormat; why = `content-type "${hint.contentType}"`; }%0A    else { format = 'csv'; why = 'assumed delimited text'; }%0A  }%0A  log(`Format detection: ${why} → ${format} (ext=${hint.ext || 'none'}, content-type="${hint.contentType || 'none'}")`);%0A  return { format, ...hint };%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: delimited text (CSV, TSV, semicolon/pipe) ---- */%0Afunction parseDelimitedText(text, format) {%0A  const t = String(text).replace(/^\uFEFF/, '').trim();%0A  const res = Papa.parse(t, { skipEmptyLines: 'greedy', delimiter: format === 'tsv' ? '\t' : '' });%0A  if (res.errors.length) warn('PapaParse reported errors:', res.errors.slice(0, 3));%0A  const delim = (res.meta && res.meta.delimiter) || ',';%0A  const rows = res.data.map(r => (Array.isArray(r) ? r : [r]).map(c => String(c ?? '')));%0A  log(`Parsed ${formatLabel(format)} text (${text.length} chars) with PapaParse — delimiter ${JSON.stringify(delim)}, ${rows.length} rows`);%0A  return rows;%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: workbooks (XLSX / XLS / ODS / XLSB) via SheetJS ---- */%0Aasync function parseWorkbook(buf, sheetPick) {%0A  log(`Parsing workbook (${buf.byteLength} bytes) with SheetJS${sheetPick ? `, sheet "${sheetPick}"` : ''}`);%0A  // `await` on purpose: the real SheetJS resolves synchronously, but a%0A  // dependency-free reader (the bookmarklet build) inflates asynchronously.%0A  const wb = await XLSX.read(buf, { type: 'array' });%0A  const name = sheetPick && wb.SheetNames.includes(sheetPick) ? sheetPick : wb.SheetNames[0];%0A  const ws = wb.Sheets[name];%0A  const rows = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(ws, { header: 1, raw: false, defval: '' })%0A    .map(row => row.map(c => String(c ?? '')));%0A  log(`Workbook parsed: ${wb.SheetNames.length} sheet(s), loaded "${name}" — ${rows.length} rows`);%0A  return { rows, sheetName: name };%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: DOCX (Word) ---- */%0Aconst WORDPROC_NS = 'http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main';%0A/** A Word table row is <w:tr>, a cell <w:tc>, and text lives in <w:t> runs inside%0A    <w:p> paragraphs — so a cell's text is that cell's runs joined. Tables are what%0A    a link list lives in; a document without one falls back to a row per paragraph%0A    (cells split on tabs), which is exactly what a pasted-from-Word list looks like. */%0Aasync function parseDocx(buf) {%0A  const entry = zipEntries(buf).get('word/document.xml');%0A  if (!entry) throw new Error('this .docx has no word/document.xml — is it a Word file, or something else renamed?');%0A  const xml = await zipEntryText(buf, entry);%0A  const dom = new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml, 'application/xml');%0A  if (dom.querySelector('parsererror')) throw new Error('word/document.xml is not readable XML — the file may be damaged');%0A  const runs = (el) => Array.from(el.getElementsByTagNameNS(WORDPROC_NS, 't')).map(t => t.textContent || '').join('').trim();%0A  const tables = Array.from(dom.getElementsByTagNameNS(WORDPROC_NS, 'tbl'));%0A  if (tables.length) {%0A    const rows = [];%0A    for (const tbl of tables) {%0A      for (const tr of Array.from(tbl.getElementsByTagNameNS(WORDPROC_NS, 'tr'))) {%0A        rows.push(Array.from(tr.children)%0A          .filter(c => c.namespaceURI === WORDPROC_NS && c.localName === 'tc')%0A          .map(runs));%0A      }%0A    }%0A    log(`DOCX parsed: ${tables.length} table(s), ${rows.length} rows, ${Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.length), 0)} columns`);%0A    if (!rows.length) throw new Error('the Word table in this document is empty');%0A    return rows;%0A  }%0A  const rows = Array.from(dom.getElementsByTagNameNS(WORDPROC_NS, 'p'))%0A    .map(p => runs(p).split('\t').map(s => s.trim()))%0A    .filter(r => r.some(c => c));%0A  log(`DOCX parsed: no table — ${rows.length} paragraph rows`);%0A  if (!rows.length) throw new Error('this .docx has no text to read');%0A  return rows;%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: Markdown (task lists, pipe tables, link lists) ----%0A   Markdown is plain text, so this needs no library — the same reason DOCX needed%0A   none — which means every build gets it, including the zero-library bookmarklet.%0A   A task list is already a table with the four columns Turnstone wants: the task,%0A   its link, the checkbox and the trailing note. So the list parser emits a matrix%0A   shaped exactly like the CSV fixture's, and nothing downstream has to know that a%0A   checkbox was ever involved. */%0Aconst MD_FENCE_RE = /^\s*(?:```|~~~)/;%0Aconst MD_TASK_RE = /^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+\[([ xX])\]\s+(.*)$/;%0Aconst MD_ITEM_RE = /^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+(\S.*)$/;%0Aconst MD_HEADING_RE = /^\s{0,3}%23{1,6}\s/;%0A/* One scan for every link shape markdown actually carries: [label](target),%0A   <autolink>, an explicit scheme URL, a bare http/www URL, and a bare address.%0A   Order matters — the scheme alternative has to run before the bare-address one, or%0A   "mailto:ada@example.com" would match as "ada@example.com" and leave "mailto:"%0A   stranded in the task's text. */%0Aconst MD_LINK_SCAN = /\[([^\]]*)\]\(\s*([^\s)]+)(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\s*\)|<((?:https?|mailto|tel|sms):[^>\s]+)>|(mailto:[a-z0-9._%25+'\-]+@[a-z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9\-]+)+)(?:\?[^\s]*)?|((?:tel|sms):[+\d][\d\s().\u2011\-\/]{4,}\d)(?:\?[^\s]*)?|((?:https?:\/\/|www\.)[^\s<>()\[\]`*_]+)|([a-z0-9._%25+'\-]+@[a-z0-9\-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9\-]+)+)/gi;%0Aconst MD_LINK_RE = /\[([^\]]*)\]\(\s*([^\s)]+)(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\s*\)/g;%0A/* Separators a task line uses to set its name and note apart from its link. */%0Aconst MD_TRIM_RE = /^[\s·•\-–—:]+|[\s·•\-–—:]+$/g;%0A%0A/** Markdown's decoration, removed: code spans, bold, italic, backslash escapes. */%0Afunction mdStripInline(s) {%0A  return String(s ?? '')%0A    .replace(/`([^`]*)`/g, '$1')%0A    .replace(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g, '$1')%0A    .replace(/__([^_]+)__/g, '$1')%0A    .replace(/(^|[\s(])\*([^*\n]+)\*/g, '$1$2')%0A    .replace(/(^|[\s(])_([^_\n]+)_/g, '$1$2')%0A    .replace(/\\([\\`*_{}\[\]()%23+\-.!|>])/g, '$1');%0A}%0A%0A/** Every link on a line, in order, with its exact span in the raw text. */%0Afunction mdLinks(text) {%0A  const out = [];%0A  MD_LINK_SCAN.lastIndex = 0;   // the scan regex is shared, so its cursor is reset per call%0A  let m;%0A  while ((m = MD_LINK_SCAN.exec(text))) {%0A    out.push({%0A      start: m.index,%0A      end: m.index + m[0].length,%0A      label: m[1] !== undefined ? mdStripInline(m[1]).trim() : '',%0A      target: (m[2] || m[3] || m[4] || m[5] || m[6] || m[7] || '').trim(),%0A    });%0A  }%0A  return out;%0A}%0A%0A/** A markdown link's target may carry its own kind (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`) and a%0A    query. The matrix wants the bare *value*, so the app's own value predicates%0A    recognise it and the href can be rebuilt from the kind at render time. */%0Afunction normalizeLinkTarget(target) {%0A  const t = String(target ?? '').trim().replace(/^<(.*)>$/, '$1');%0A  const m = t.match(/^(?:mailto|tel|sms):([^?%23]*)/i);%0A  return m ? (m[1].trim() || t) : t;%0A}%0A%0A/** A pipe-table cell: decoration stripped, a lone link resolved to its target (so a%0A    URL column holds a URL), an inline link in prose reduced to its label. */%0Afunction mdInlineCell(raw) {%0A  const text = mdStripInline(raw).trim();%0A  const links = mdLinks(text);%0A  if (links.length === 1 && !text.slice(0, links[0].start).trim() && !text.slice(links[0].end).trim()) {%0A    const target = normalizeLinkTarget(links[0].target);%0A    return linkKindOf(target) ? target : (links[0].label || target);%0A  }%0A  return text.replace(MD_LINK_RE, (whole, label, target) => label.trim() || normalizeLinkTarget(target));%0A}%0A%0A/** `| a | b |` → ['a','b'], honouring `\|` escapes and stripping the outer pipes. */%0Afunction mdSplitRow(line) {%0A  const t = String(line).trim().replace(/^\||\|$/g, '');%0A  const cells = [];%0A  let cur = '';%0A  for (let i = 0; i < t.length; i++) {%0A    if (t[i] === '\\' && t[i + 1] === '|') { cur += '|'; i++; continue; }%0A    if (t[i] === '|') { cells.push(cur); cur = ''; continue; }%0A    cur += t[i];%0A  }%0A  cells.push(cur);%0A  return cells.map(mdInlineCell);%0A}%0A/** The `|---|:--:|` row that makes a stack of pipes a table rather than a paragraph. */%0Afunction mdIsDelimiterRow(line) {%0A  const t = String(line).trim();%0A  if (!t.includes('-')) return false;%0A  return t.replace(/^\||\|$/g, '').split('|').every(c => /^:?-{2,}:?$/.test(c.trim()));%0A}%0A/** Lines outside fenced code blocks — a URL in a code fence is an example, not a task. */%0Afunction mdUnfencedLines(text) {%0A  const out = [];%0A  let fenced = false;%0A  for (const line of String(text).replace(/^\uFEFF/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) {%0A    if (MD_FENCE_RE.test(line)) { fenced = !fenced; continue; }%0A    if (!fenced) out.push(line);%0A  }%0A  return out;%0A}%0Afunction mdFindTable(lines) {%0A  for (let i = 0; i + 1 < lines.length; i++) {%0A    if (!lines[i].includes('|') || !mdIsDelimiterRow(lines[i + 1])) continue;%0A    const header = mdSplitRow(lines[i]);%0A    const rows = [header];%0A    for (let j = i + 2; j < lines.length; j++) {%0A      if (!lines[j].includes('|')) break;%0A      if (mdIsDelimiterRow(lines[j])) continue;%0A      const cells = mdSplitRow(lines[j]);%0A      while (cells.length < header.length) cells.push('');%0A      rows.push(cells.slice(0, header.length));%0A    }%0A    log(`Markdown parsed: pipe table — ${header.length} column(s), ${rows.length - 1} row(s)`);%0A    return rows;%0A  }%0A  return null;%0A}%0A%0A/** List item → { name, link, checked, note }. The first link ends the name and%0A    starts the note, which is why a note containing its own em dash survives. */%0Afunction mdListItem(body, box) {%0A  const links = mdLinks(body);%0A  if (!links.length) return { name: mdStripInline(body).replace(MD_TRIM_RE, ''), link: '', checked: box, note: '' };%0A  const first = links[0];%0A  let before = mdStripInline(body.slice(0, first.start)).replace(MD_TRIM_RE, '');%0A  let after = mdStripInline(body.slice(first.end)).replace(MD_TRIM_RE, '');%0A  /* `- Task (https://link)` — the link sat inside brackets, so one half of the pair%0A     lands in the name and the other in the note. Drop them together, and only when%0A     they actually pair up, so a note that legitimately starts with "(" survives. */%0A  if (/[([]$/.test(before) && /^[)\]]/.test(after)) {%0A    before = before.replace(/[([]$/, '').trim();%0A    after = after.replace(/^[)\]]/, '').trim();%0A  }%0A  const target = normalizeLinkTarget(first.target);%0A  const link = linkKindOf(target) ? target : (linkKindOf(first.label) ? first.label : target);%0A  return { name: before || first.label || link, link, checked: box, note: after };%0A}%0A%0A/** Items → matrix, with only the columns the file actually has. A bare-URL list%0A    gets one column; a task list gets all four, headed exactly like the CSV fixture. */%0Afunction mdMatrix(items) {%0A  const hasLink = items.some(it => it.link);%0A  const hasBox = items.some(it => it.checked !== null);%0A  const hasNote = items.some(it => it.note);%0A  const hasNames = items.some(it => it.name && it.name !== it.link);%0A  const cols = [];%0A  if (hasNames) cols.push(['Name', it => it.name]);%0A  if (hasLink) cols.push(['URL', it => it.link]);%0A  if (hasBox) cols.push(['Status', it => (it.checked ? 'complete' : 'incomplete')]);%0A  if (hasNote) cols.push(['Notes', it => it.note]);%0A  if (!cols.length) cols.push(['Name', it => it.name]);%0A  log(`Markdown parsed: ${items.length} item(s) → ${cols.map(([h]) => h).join(' / ')}`);%0A  return [cols.map(([h]) => h), ...items.map(it => cols.map(([, get]) => get(it)))];%0A}%0A%0Afunction parseMarkdownText(text) {%0A  const lines = mdUnfencedLines(text);%0A  const table = mdFindTable(lines);%0A  if (table) return table;%0A  const listed = [], loose = [];%0A  for (const line of lines) {%0A    const task = line.match(MD_TASK_RE);%0A    const bullet = task ? null : line.match(MD_ITEM_RE);%0A    if (task) listed.push(mdListItem(task[2].trim(), task[1].toLowerCase() === 'x'));%0A    else if (bullet) {%0A      const item = mdListItem(bullet[1].trim(), null);%0A      /* A bullet is only a task if it points somewhere — that is what keeps a%0A         README's bulleted prose out of the queue. */%0A      if (item.link) listed.push(item);%0A    } else if (!MD_HEADING_RE.test(line) && line.trim()) {%0A      const item = mdListItem(line.trim(), null);%0A      if (item.link) loose.push(item);%0A    }%0A  }%0A  /* A list wins outright when there is one: a document's stray prose links should%0A     not be appended to the queue its list describes. */%0A  const items = listed.length ? listed : loose;%0A  if (!items.length) throw new Error('nothing to queue in this markdown file — it has no table, no list and no links');%0A  return mdMatrix(items);%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: JSON (array of objects, array of arrays, wrapped array, NDJSON) ---- */%0Afunction jsonScalar(v) {%0A  if (v === null || v === undefined) return '';%0A  return typeof v === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(v) : String(v);%0A}%0A%0A/** Array of objects → header row (union of keys, first-seen order) + data rows. */%0Afunction jsonObjectsToMatrix(objs) {%0A  const keys = [], seen = new Set();%0A  for (const o of objs) {%0A    if (!o || typeof o !== 'object' || Array.isArray(o)) continue;%0A    for (const k of Object.keys(o)) if (!seen.has(k)) { seen.add(k); keys.push(k); }%0A  }%0A  if (!keys.length) return null;%0A  return [keys, ...objs.map(o => keys.map(k => jsonScalar(o && typeof o === 'object' ? o[k] : '')))];%0A}%0A%0A/** First array nested anywhere inside an object, e.g. {items:[…]} or {data:{rows:[…]}}. */%0Afunction findJsonArray(value, depth = 0) {%0A  if (depth > 4 || !value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return null;%0A  for (const v of Object.values(value)) if (Array.isArray(v) && v.length) return v;%0A  for (const v of Object.values(value)) {%0A    const hit = findJsonArray(v, depth + 1);%0A    if (hit) return hit;%0A  }%0A  return null;%0A}%0A%0Afunction jsonToMatrix(value) {%0A  let v = value;%0A  if (!Array.isArray(v)) {%0A    if (v && typeof v === 'object') {%0A      const inner = findJsonArray(v);%0A      if (inner) { log('JSON: unwrapped a single nested array (e.g. {items:[…]})'); v = inner; }%0A      else {%0A        const vals = Object.values(v);%0A        if (vals.length && vals.every(x => x && typeof x === 'object' && !Array.isArray(x))) {%0A          log(`JSON: an object map with ${vals.length} entries → records, keys kept as _key`);%0A          return jsonObjectsToMatrix(Object.entries(v).map(([k, o]) => ({ _key: k, ...o })));%0A        }%0A        log('JSON: a single object → one record');%0A        return jsonObjectsToMatrix([v]);%0A      }%0A    } else {%0A      return [['Value'], [jsonScalar(v)]];%0A    }%0A  }%0A  if (!v.length) return [];%0A  if (v.every(Array.isArray)) {%0A    log(`JSON: array of ${v.length} arrays → rows verbatim`);%0A    return v.map(r => r.map(jsonScalar));%0A  }%0A  if (v.every(x => x && typeof x === 'object' && !Array.isArray(x))) {%0A    const m = jsonObjectsToMatrix(v);%0A    if (m) { log(`JSON: array of ${v.length} objects → ${m[0].length} columns`); return m; }%0A  }%0A  log(`JSON: array of ${v.length} scalars → single Value column`);%0A  return [['Value'], ...v.map(x => [jsonScalar(x)])];%0A}%0A%0Afunction parseJsonText(text) {%0A  let parsed;%0A  try {%0A    parsed = JSON.parse(String(text).replace(/^\uFEFF/, ''));%0A  } catch (e) {%0A    // JSON Lines / NDJSON: one object per line is a very common export shape.%0A    const lines = String(text).trim().split(/\r?\n/).filter(l => l.trim());%0A    const objs = lines.length > 1 && lines.every(l => /^\s*[\[{]/.test(l))%0A      ? lines.map(l => { try { return JSON.parse(l); } catch { return null; } })%0A      : [];%0A    if (!objs.length || !objs.every(Boolean)) throw new Error(`invalid JSON (${e.message})`);%0A    log(`JSON.parse failed — recovered as NDJSON (${objs.length} lines)`);%0A    return jsonToMatrix(objs);%0A  }%0A  const rows = jsonToMatrix(parsed);%0A  log(`JSON parsed: ${rows.length} rows × ${rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0)} cols`);%0A  return rows;%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: HTML tables (and, for local picks, plain link lists) ---- */%0A/** Rows of a <table> → rectangular grid, honouring rowspan/colspan. */%0Afunction tableToMatrix(table) {%0A  const own = (el) => el.closest('table') === table; // ignore nested tables%0A  const trs = [...table.querySelectorAll('tr')].filter(own);%0A  const grid = [];%0A  trs.forEach((tr, r) => {%0A    grid[r] = grid[r] || [];%0A    let col = 0;%0A    for (const cell of [...tr.querySelectorAll('th, td')].filter(own)) {%0A      while (grid[r][col] !== undefined) col++;%0A      const cs = Math.max(1, parseInt(cell.getAttribute('colspan') || '1', 10) || 1);%0A      const rs = Math.max(1, parseInt(cell.getAttribute('rowspan') || '1', 10) || 1);%0A      const text = cell.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();%0A      for (let dr = 0; dr < rs; dr++) {%0A        grid[r + dr] = grid[r + dr] || [];%0A        for (let dc = 0; dc < cs; dc++) {%0A          if (grid[r + dr][col + dc] === undefined) grid[r + dr][col + dc] = dr === 0 && dc === 0 ? text : '';%0A        }%0A      }%0A      col += cs;%0A    }%0A  });%0A  return grid%0A    .filter(row => row && row.some(c => c !== undefined && c !== ''))%0A    .map(row => { const out = []; for (let i = 0; i < row.length; i++) out[i] = String(row[i] ?? ''); return out; });%0A}%0A%0Afunction parseHtmlText(text, { allowLinkFallback = true } = {}) {%0A  // parseFromString yields an inert document: no scripts run, no images fetch.%0A  const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(String(text), 'text/html');%0A  // Only consider top-level tables; a nested table is almost always layout filler.%0A  const tables = [...doc.querySelectorAll('table')].filter(t => !(t.parentElement && t.parentElement.closest('table')));%0A  let best = null, bestScore = 0;%0A  for (const t of tables) {%0A    const m = tableToMatrix(t);%0A    const score = m.length * m.reduce((w, r) => Math.max(w, r.length), 0);%0A    if (score > bestScore) { bestScore = score; best = m; }%0A  }%0A  if (best && best.length >= 2) {%0A    log(`HTML parsed: picked the largest of ${tables.length} table(s) — ${best.length} rows × ${best.reduce((w, r) => Math.max(w, r.length), 0)} cols`);%0A    return best;%0A  }%0A  if (!allowLinkFallback) throw new Error('that URL returned a web page with no data table in it');%0A  // Saved bookmarks pages and link round-ups are lists, not tables.%0A  const seen = new Set(), links = [];%0A  for (const a of doc.querySelectorAll('a[href]')) {%0A    const href = a.getAttribute('href') || '';%0A    if (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(href) || seen.has(href)) continue;%0A    seen.add(href);%0A    links.push([a.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() || href, href]);%0A  }%0A  if (links.length) {%0A    log(`HTML parsed: no usable table — harvested ${links.length} http(s) link(s) from <a href>`);%0A    return [['Name', 'URL'], ...links];%0A  }%0A  throw new Error('no <table> rows and no http(s) links found');%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: XML (RSS/Atom feeds, sitemaps, OPML, generic record lists) ---- */%0Aconst XML_RECORD_TAGS = /^(item|entry|record|row|link|url|post|article|result|job|task|page|doc|node|member|place|event|product|book)$/i;%0A%0A/** The element name that most looks like a repeated record in this document.%0A    Record containers (elements that hold fields) beat leaf elements — otherwise an%0A    RSS feed would tabulate its <link> elements instead of its <item> elements. */%0Afunction pickXmlRecordTag(doc) {%0A  const seen = new Map(); // tagName → { count, containers }%0A  for (const el of doc.querySelectorAll('*')) {%0A    const n = el.tagName;%0A    const rec = seen.get(n) || { count: 0, containers: 0 };%0A    rec.count++;%0A    if (el.children.length) rec.containers++;%0A    seen.set(n, rec);%0A  }%0A  const repeated = [...seen.entries()]%0A    .filter(([n, r]) => r.count >= 2 && !/^(html|head|body|script|style)$/i.test(n))%0A    .map(([n, r]) => ({ tag: n, ...r, known: XML_RECORD_TAGS.test(n) }));%0A  if (!repeated.length) return null;%0A  const rank = (a, b) => (b.known - a.known) || (b.count - a.count);%0A  const containers = repeated.filter(r => r.containers === r.count).sort(rank);%0A  if (containers.length) return containers[0].tag;%0A  return repeated.sort(rank)[0].tag;%0A}%0A%0A/** Text of a leaf element — falling back to its url-ish attribute (Atom <link href>). */%0Afunction xmlLeafValue(el) {%0A  const text = el.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();%0A  if (text) return text;%0A  for (const a of ['href', 'url', 'src', 'loc']) {%0A    const v = el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute(a);%0A    if (v) return v;%0A  }%0A  return [...(el.attributes || [])].map(a => a.value).join(' ');%0A}%0A%0Afunction xmlElementToRecord(el) {%0A  const rec = {};%0A  // Attributes first so href/url land in an early column.%0A  for (const attr of el.attributes || []) rec[attr.name] = attr.value;%0A  const kids = [...el.children];%0A  if (!kids.length && !Object.keys(rec).length) rec.value = xmlLeafValue(el);%0A  for (const k of kids) {%0A    const val = k.children.length ? JSON.stringify(xmlToPlain(k)) : xmlLeafValue(k);%0A    rec[k.tagName] = rec[k.tagName] === undefined ? val : `${rec[k.tagName]}; ${val}`;%0A  }%0A  return rec;%0A}%0Afunction xmlToPlain(el) {%0A  const o = {};%0A  for (const attr of el.attributes || []) o[attr.name] = attr.value;%0A  const kids = [...el.children];%0A  if (!kids.length) o.value = xmlLeafValue(el);%0A  for (const k of kids) o[k.tagName] = k.children.length ? xmlToPlain(k) : xmlLeafValue(k);%0A  return o;%0A}%0A%0Afunction parseXmlText(text) {%0A  const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(String(text), 'application/xml');%0A  if (doc.querySelector('parsererror')) throw new Error('XML is not well-formed');%0A  const tag = pickXmlRecordTag(doc);%0A  if (!tag) throw new Error('no repeated record elements to turn into rows');%0A  const els = [...doc.querySelectorAll(tag)];%0A  log(`XML parsed: ${els.length} <${tag}> record element(s)`);%0A  const recs = els.map(xmlElementToRecord);%0A  const keys = [];%0A  for (const r of recs) for (const k of Object.keys(r)) if (!keys.includes(k)) keys.push(k);%0A  return [keys, ...recs.map(r => keys.map(k => jsonScalar(r[k])))];%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Parser: email (.eml / .mht) ------------------------------------------ */%0A/* An .eml is a MIME message, and a queue very often arrives as one: someone%0A   forwards "here is this week's list, please work through it", or a portal emails%0A   a digest. Two things make it worth reading properly rather than refusing:%0A%0A     1. the message body is HTML or text, and both parsers already exist; and%0A     2. a forwarded queue usually has the *spreadsheet attached*, so the real%0A        payload is a base64 part that our own detector can already open.%0A%0A   Everything below works in "binary string" space — a JS string whose character%0A   codes are the file's bytes, 1:1. That keeps one representation from the raw%0A   file down to the part bodies, so base64, quoted-printable and a declared%0A   charset are all decodable without guessing at any point.%0A%0A   Unlike every other parser here, this one is async: recursing into an attached%0A   workbook means calling back into parseDetected. */%0Aconst MIME_MAX_DEPTH = 8;%0Afunction bytesToBinary(buf) {%0A  const b = new Uint8Array(buf);%0A  let s = '';%0A  for (let i = 0; i < b.length; i += 0x8000) s += String.fromCharCode.apply(null, b.subarray(i, i + 0x8000));%0A  return s;%0A}%0Afunction binaryToBytes(bin) {%0A  const a = new Uint8Array(bin.length);%0A  for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) a[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i) & 0xff;%0A  return a;%0A}%0A/** Charset labels we will hand to TextDecoder, aliased to the canonical name.%0A    Anything unrecognized falls back to UTF-8, which is the safe modern default. */%0Aconst CHARSET_ALIAS = {%0A  'utf8': 'utf-8', 'utf-8': 'utf-8', 'us-ascii': 'utf-8', 'ascii': 'utf-8', 'unicode-1-1-utf-8': 'utf-8',%0A  'latin1': 'windows-1252', 'latin-1': 'windows-1252', 'iso-8859-1': 'windows-1252', 'iso8859-1': 'windows-1252',%0A  'iso-8859-15': 'iso-8859-15', 'cp1252': 'windows-1252', 'windows-1252': 'windows-1252',%0A  'utf-16': 'utf-16le', 'utf-16le': 'utf-16le', 'utf-16be': 'utf-16be',%0A  'gb2312': 'gbk', 'gbk': 'gbk', 'big5': 'big5', 'shift_jis': 'shift_jis', 'sjis': 'shift_jis', 'euc-kr': 'euc-kr',%0A};%0Afunction charsetDecode(bin, charset) {%0A  const label = CHARSET_ALIAS[String(charset || '').trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^"|"$/g, '')] || 'utf-8';%0A  try { return new TextDecoder(label).decode(binaryToBytes(bin)); }%0A  catch (e) { warn(`Unknown charset "${charset}" — decoded as UTF-8`, e); return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(binaryToBytes(bin)); }%0A}%0A/** `=XX` escapes and soft line breaks (a trailing `=`) — quoted-printable. */%0Afunction decodeQuotedPrintable(bin) {%0A  return String(bin)%0A    .replace(/=\r?\n/g, '')                      // soft line break: the line continues%0A    .replace(/=([0-9a-f]{2})/gi, (_, h) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h, 16)));%0A}%0A/** Header fields, with folded continuations joined and names lower-cased. */%0Afunction mimeHeaderFields(block) {%0A  const map = new Map();%0A  let last = null;%0A  for (const line of String(block).split(/\r?\n/)) {%0A    if (/^[ \t]/.test(line) && last) { map.set(last, map.get(last) + ' ' + line.trim()); continue; }%0A    const m = line.match(/^([!-9;-~]+):[ \t]?(.*)$/);%0A    if (!m) continue;%0A    last = m[1].toLowerCase();%0A    map.set(last, m[2].trim());%0A  }%0A  return map;%0A}%0A/** Split a MIME entity at the first blank line: everything above is headers. */%0Afunction splitMimeEntity(text) {%0A  const m = /\r?\n\r?\n/.exec(text);%0A  if (!m) return { headers: mimeHeaderFields(text), body: '' };%0A  return { headers: mimeHeaderFields(text.slice(0, m.index)), body: text.slice(m.index + m[0].length) };%0A}%0Afunction mimeParams(value) {%0A  const out = {};%0A  const re = /;\s*([a-z0-9*_-]+(?:\*\d+)?)\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|([^;]*))/gi;%0A  let m;%0A  while ((m = re.exec(String(value)))) out[m[1].toLowerCase()] = (m[2] !== undefined ? m[2] : (m[3] || '')).trim();%0A  return out;%0A}%0Afunction mimeContentType(headers) {%0A  const raw = headers.get('content-type') || 'text/plain';%0A  return { type: (raw.split(';')[0] || '').trim().toLowerCase(), params: mimeParams(raw) };%0A}%0A/** A filename, honouring the RFC 2231 form Outlook writes for non-ASCII names. */%0Afunction mimeFilename(part) {%0A  const disp = part.headers.get('content-disposition') || '';%0A  const p = mimeParams(disp);%0A  if (p['filename*0*'] || p['filename*']) {%0A    const raw = p['filename*'] || p['filename*0*'];%0A    // utf-8''na%25C3%25AFve.csv%0A    const m = /^([^']*)'[^']*'(.*)$/.exec(raw);%0A    if (m) { try { return decodeURIComponent(m[2]); } catch (e) {} }%0A  }%0A  return p.filename || part.params.name || '';%0A}%0A/** Walk the boundary tree, flattening to leaf entities. */%0Afunction collectMimeParts(text, depth, out) {%0A  if (depth > MIME_MAX_DEPTH) { warn('MIME nesting too deep — stopping'); return; }%0A  const { headers, body } = splitMimeEntity(text);%0A  const { type, params } = mimeContentType(headers);%0A  if (type.startsWith('multipart/') && params.boundary) {%0A    for (const chunk of splitMimeParts(body, params.boundary)) collectMimeParts(chunk, depth + 1, out);%0A    return;%0A  }%0A  out.push({ headers, body, type, params });%0A}%0A/** Split a multipart body on its boundary. The closing `--boundary--` ends the%0A    list; the CRLF that precedes a delimiter belongs to the delimiter, not to the%0A    part, which is why the match starts with it. */%0Afunction splitMimeParts(body, boundary) {%0A  const esc = String(boundary).replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');%0A  const re = new RegExp('(?:^|\\r?\\n)--' + esc + '(--)?[^\\r\\n]*', 'g');%0A  const marks = [];%0A  let m;%0A  while ((m = re.exec(body))) marks.push({ start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, close: !!m[1] });%0A  const parts = [];%0A  for (let i = 0; i < marks.length; i++) {%0A    if (marks[i].close) break;%0A    /* One leading CRLF belongs to the delimiter line, so it is not part of the%0A       part that follows — and leaving it there would make the part's own first%0A       line look like a blank one, i.e. an empty header block. */%0A    const chunk = body.slice(marks[i].end, marks[i + 1] ? marks[i + 1].start : body.length);%0A    parts.push(chunk.replace(/^\r?\n/, ''));%0A  }%0A  return parts;%0A}%0A/** A leaf part's content, transfer-decoded then charset-decoded. */%0Afunction decodeMimePart(part) {%0A  const enc = (part.headers.get('content-transfer-encoding') || '').toLowerCase().trim();%0A  let bin = part.body;%0A  if (enc === 'base64') { try { bin = atob(bin.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9+/=]/g, '')); } catch (e) { warn('base64 part did not decode cleanly', e); } }%0A  else if (enc === 'quoted-printable') bin = decodeQuotedPrintable(bin);%0A  return charsetDecode(bin, part.params.charset);%0A}%0A/** Is this a *list*, or just prose that happens to have line breaks? Without this%0A    an email that says "Hi, three things" would parse as a three-row table of%0A    sentences — confidently wrong, which is the one outcome this app avoids. */%0Afunction plausibleList(rows) {%0A  const body = rows.filter(r => r.some(c => String(c ?? '').trim()));%0A  if (body.length < 2) return false;%0A  const width = body.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0);%0A  if (width >= 2) return true;%0A  const vals = body.map(r => String(r[0] ?? '').trim()).filter(Boolean);%0A  return vals.length >= 2 && vals.every(v => linkKindOf(v));%0A}%0A/** A text/plain body: markdown if it is markdown, otherwise delimited. */%0Afunction parseEmlPlainText(text) {%0A  const guess = sniffTextFormat(String(text).slice(0, 4096));%0A  if (guess === 'md') return parseMarkdownText(text);%0A  return parseDelimitedText(text, /\t/.test(text) ? 'tsv' : 'csv');%0A}%0A%0A/** Is this ambiguity-prone text a *table*? Stricter than `plausibleList`, and%0A    both callers are the cases where prose can masquerade as data:%0A%0A      - a text/plain email body, which is prose by default — splitting "Hi,\n\nThe%0A        queue for this week's run is attached. Ten items, four of them" on commas%0A        yields rows of wildly different lengths; and%0A      - a paste, where the same paragraph arrives through the same door, and%0A        loading it would silently replace the queue the user is working through.%0A%0A    So it has to be *rectangular* — every row the same width — or a single column%0A    of nothing but link-shaped values. A real table from Excel, Sheets or a portal%0A    is rectangular because the cells are there whether or not they hold anything. */%0Afunction plausibleTable(rows) {%0A  if (!plausibleList(rows)) return false;%0A  const body = rows.filter(r => r.some(c => String(c ?? '').trim()));%0A  const widths = new Set(body.map(r => r.length));%0A  if (widths.size !== 1) return false;%0A  const width = [...widths][0];%0A  return width >= 2 || body.every(r => linkKindOf(String(r[0] ?? '').trim()));%0A}%0A%0A/** Read an .eml / .mht: the best body part that yields a list, else an attachment. */%0Aasync function parseEmlText(bin, { depth = 0, sheetPick = null } = {}) {%0A  const parts = [];%0A  collectMimeParts(bin, 0, parts);%0A  const bodies = { 'text/html': [], 'text/plain': [] };%0A  const attachments = [];%0A  for (const p of parts) {%0A    const disp = (p.headers.get('content-disposition') || '').toLowerCase();%0A    const filename = mimeFilename(p);%0A    if (/^\s*attachment/.test(disp) || (!p.type.startsWith('text/') && filename)) { attachments.push(Object.assign(p, { filename })); continue; }%0A    if (bodies[p.type]) bodies[p.type].push(p);%0A  }%0A  log(`Email parsed: ${parts.length} MIME part(s) — ${bodies['text/html'].length} HTML body, ${bodies['text/plain'].length} text body, ${attachments.length} attachment(s)`);%0A%0A  /* Bodies first: a forward often carries both the table *and* the file, and the%0A     table is the more deliberate statement of the list. HTML before plain,%0A     because the plain part of a multipart/alternative is its degraded copy. */%0A  for (const p of [...bodies['text/html'], ...bodies['text/plain']]) {%0A    let text;%0A    try { text = decodeMimePart(p); } catch (e) { warn('Could not decode a body part', e); continue; }%0A    if (!text.trim()) continue;%0A    let rows;%0A    try {%0A      rows = p.type === 'text/html'%0A        ? (HAS_DOMPARSER ? parseHtmlText(text, { allowLinkFallback: true }) : null)%0A        : parseEmlPlainText(text);%0A    } catch (e) { log(`Body part (${p.type}) had no list: ${e.message}`); continue; }%0A    const acceptable = p.type === 'text/html' ? plausibleList(rows) : plausibleTable(rows);%0A    if (rows && acceptable) {%0A      log(`Email body used: ${p.type} body part → ${rows.length} row(s)`);%0A      return { rows, from: `${p.type} body` };%0A    }%0A    if (rows) log(`Body part (${p.type}) parsed but is not list-shaped — ignoring it`);%0A  }%0A%0A  /* Then attachments: "here is the queue" with the export attached. */%0A  if (depth < 1) {%0A    for (const a of attachments) {%0A      if (!a.filename) continue;%0A      const ext = (a.filename.match(/\.([a-z0-9]{1,10})$/i) || [])[1];%0A      if (!ext || !EXT_FORMAT[ext.toLowerCase()]) { log(`Skipping attachment "${a.filename}" (no reader for it)`); continue; }%0A      const bytes = binaryToBytes(decodeMimePartBinary(a));%0A      if (bytes.byteLength < 8) continue;%0A      const det = detectFormat(bytes.buffer, a.filename, a.headers.get('content-type') || '');%0A      if (det.format === 'eml') continue;   // an attached message would just recurse%0A      try {%0A        const { rows, format } = await parseDetected(bytes.buffer, det, sheetPick, { allowLinkFallback: false });%0A        if (plausibleList(rows)) { log(`Email attachment used: "${a.filename}" → ${format}, ${rows.length} row(s)`); return { rows, from: `attachment ${a.filename}` }; }%0A        log(`Attachment "${a.filename}" parsed as ${format} but is not list-shaped`);%0A      } catch (e) { log(`Attachment "${a.filename}" could not be read: ${e.message}`); }%0A    }%0A  }%0A  if (!parts.length) throw new Error('this file is not a readable email message');%0A  throw new Error('no list in this email — no table, no link list, and no readable attachment in it');%0A}%0A/** The raw transfer-decoded bytes of a part (attachments need bytes, not text). */%0Afunction decodeMimePartBinary(part) {%0A  const enc = (part.headers.get('content-transfer-encoding') || '').toLowerCase().trim();%0A  if (enc === 'base64') { try { return atob(part.body.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9+/=]/g, '')); } catch (e) { warn('base64 attachment did not decode cleanly', e); return part.body; } }%0A  if (enc === 'quoted-printable') return decodeQuotedPrintable(part.body);%0A  return part.body;%0A}%0A%0A/* ======================================================================%0A   Workspace links — a whole list carried inside a URL%0A   ======================================================================%0A   This is the one container that has no file behind it: an agent (or a person)%0A   hands over a link, and the list is already there. It is a *format* concern like%0A   every other reader in this file, so it lives here rather than in the boot code.%0A%0A   Two encodings, for two different callers:%0A%0A     %23data=<text>   the list as percent-encoded text. Readable, debuggable, and the%0A                    one a language model or a person can write by hand.%0A     %23zdata=<text>  the same text deflated (raw) then base64url'd, no padding.
