Four%0A                    to six times smaller, which is the difference between a link%0A                    that survives a chat client and one that gets truncated. Needs%0A                    DecompressionStream to open — native, and no dependency.%0A%0A   The fragment rather than the query string is a deliberate choice with two%0A   independent reasons. A fragment is never sent to the server, so a list of client%0A   names handed over this way never lands in GitHub's access logs — which matters%0A   for an app whose whole claim is that nothing is uploaded. And it escapes the%0A   ~8 KB request-line limit that a query string is subject to (nginx's default%0A   8 KB header buffer answers anything longer with a 414), so a long list works%0A   where `?data=` would be refused by the host before our code ever ran.%0A   `?data=` is still read, for tooling that can only append a query. */%0A%0A/** Past this, a URL is being asked to be a file. Refused with a reason. */%0Aconst INLINE_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024;%0A/** Past this, a link may still work but chat clients start trimming it. Warned about. */%0Aconst INLINE_WARN_BYTES = 100 * 1024;%0A%0A/** Bytes → base64url, no padding. Chunked, because the spread operator dies at%0A    ~100k arguments and a list is bigger than that. */%0Afunction bytesToBase64Url(bytes) {%0A  let bin = '';%0A  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 0x8000) {%0A    bin += String.fromCharCode.apply(null, bytes.subarray(i, i + 0x8000));%0A  }%0A  return btoa(bin).replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');%0A}%0A%0A/** base64url → bytes. Accepts the standard alphabet and padding too, because%0A    `+` and `/` survive enough transports that people paste them in. */%0Afunction base64UrlToBytes(s) {%0A  const clean = String(s || '').replace(/[\s]/g, '').replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');%0A  const pad = clean.length %25 4 ? '='.repeat(4 - (clean.length %25 4)) : '';%0A  const bin = atob(clean + pad);%0A  const out = new Uint8Array(bin.length);%0A  for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) out[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);%0A  return out;%0A}%0A%0A/** FNV-1a, 32-bit, over the raw bytes. Small and dependency-free, which is the%0A    whole requirement — this is a "did the link arrive whole?" check, not a%0A    security primitive. */%0Afunction fnv1a32(bytes) {%0A  let h = 0x811c9dc5;%0A  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {%0A    h ^= bytes[i];%0A    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193) >>> 0;%0A  }%0A  return h >>> 0;%0A}%0A%0A/** A short integrity token for a list: its length and checksum, in base 36.%0A *%0A * Why this exists at all: a deflate stream cut at a *block* boundary inflates%0A * without error, so a link that lost its tail in a chat client or a line-wrapped%0A * post can decode to a shorter list that looks perfectly plausible. Every other%0A * failure mode here announces itself; that one does not, and a silently short%0A * queue is the worst thing this app could hand someone. Twelve characters of URL%0A * buys the ability to say "this link is not what was sent" instead. */%0Afunction inlineDigest(bytes) {%0A  return `${bytes.length.toString(36)}.${fnv1a32(bytes).toString(36)}`;%0A}%0A%0A/** Raw deflate / inflate through the platform's streams — no library, no eval. */%0Aasync function deflateRawBytes(bytes) {%0A  if (typeof CompressionStream !== 'function') throw new Error('this browser cannot compress a link (no CompressionStream)');%0A  const stream = new Blob([bytes]).stream().pipeThrough(new CompressionStream('deflate-raw'));%0A  return new Uint8Array(await new Response(stream).arrayBuffer());%0A}%0Aasync function inflateRawBytes(bytes) {%0A  if (!HAS_INFLATE) throw new Error('this browser cannot open a compressed link (no DecompressionStream)');%0A  const stream = new Blob([bytes]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'));%0A  /* The engine's own wording here is useless to a person — a truncated stream%0A     surfaces as "Failed to fetch" (a Response whose body stream errored), and%0A     "unexpected end of file" in Node. Both mean the same thing to the reader. */%0A  try {%0A    return new Uint8Array(await new Response(stream).arrayBuffer());%0A  } catch (e) {%0A    throw new Error('the compressed list could not be unpacked — a link cut short in transit is the usual reason, so ask for it to be sent again');%0A  }%0A}%0A%0A/** The parameters a workspace link may carry, from **both** the query string and%0A    the fragment (the fragment wins — that is where we put ours). Pure string work,%0A    so the Node suite can test it without a browser. */%0Afunction inlineParamsFrom(search, hash) {%0A  const into = (acc, s) => {%0A    try {%0A      new URLSearchParams(String(s || '').replace(/^[?%23]/, '')).forEach((v, k) => { acc[k] = v; });%0A    } catch (e) { warn('Could not read URL parameters:', e); }%0A    return acc;%0A  };%0A  return into(into({}, search), hash);%0A}%0A%0A/** Is this pasted text a **workspace link** — a list already inside a URL — or a%0A    plain URL for a file to fetch? The answer decides whether the app reads its own%0A    fragment or makes a network request, so it follows a rule rather than a guess:%0A%0A      1. A `zdata` payload **anywhere** is unambiguous. Nothing else in the world%0A         spells a URL parameter that way; it is this app's own name for it.%0A      2. A payload in the **fragment** is also unambiguous, and for a reason worth%0A         writing down: a fragment is never sent to a server, so it cannot be a file%0A         URL's arguments. `x.csv%23data=…` can only be about a list someone handed over.%0A      3. A `data` payload in the **query string** is genuinely ambiguous — plenty of%0A         file endpoints take `?data=…` — so it counts only when the URL is one of our%0A         own pages: same origin, path ending in `.html` (or the directory root). That%0A         is the tooling case, where something can only append a query string.%0A%0A    Pure string work, so the Node suite tests it without a browser — and every%0A    refusal carries a reason, because "why didn't my link open?" deserves an answer%0A    rather than a silent fetch of something that was never a file. */%0Afunction workspaceLinkFrom(text) {%0A  const raw = String(text || '').trim();%0A  if (!raw) return { ok: false, why: 'there was nothing to open' };%0A%0A  /* A bare `%23zdata=…` or `zdata=…` — copied on its own, which is a normal way to%0A     pass one on — is read as the fragment it is. */%0A  const bare = /^(zdata|data|sum|format|name|link|open)=/i.test(raw.replace(/^[%23?]+/, ''));%0A  let url, frag = '', query = '';%0A  try {%0A    url = bare ? new URL(location.href) : new URL(raw, location.href);%0A  } catch (e) {%0A    return { ok: false, why: 'that is not a link' };%0A  }%0A  if (bare) frag = raw.replace(/^[%23?]+/, '');%0A  else { frag = String(url.hash || '').replace(/^%23/, ''); query = String(url.search || '').replace(/^\?/, ''); }%0A%0A  const fromFrag = inlineParamsFrom('', frag);%0A  const fromQuery = inlineParamsFrom(query, '');%0A  const params = inlineParamsFrom(query, frag);          // fragment wins, as everywhere else%0A  const payload = (fromFrag.zdata || fromQuery.zdata || '').trim();%0A  const plain = (fromFrag.data || fromQuery.data || '').trim();%0A%0A  if (payload) return { ok: true, params, where: fromFrag.zdata ? 'the fragment' : 'the query string' };%0A  if (plain && fromFrag.data) return { ok: true, params, where: 'the fragment' };%0A%0A  /* The tooling case: `?data=` on one of our own pages. A `.csv` or `.json` endpoint%0A     with a `data` parameter is a file, and stays one. */%0A  const ours = !bare && url.origin === location.origin%0A    && (/\/$/.test(url.pathname) || /\.html?$/i.test(url.pathname));%0A  if (plain && fromQuery.data && ours) return { ok: true, params, where: 'the query string of one of our own pages' };%0A%0A  /* Nothing to open — but *which* nothing matters to the caller: a file URL should%0A     still go down the fetch path, while a stray paste should say what was missing. */%0A  const looksLikeUrl = /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//i.test(raw) || /^\//.test(raw) || /^[\w.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}/i.test(raw);%0A  return looksLikeUrl%0A    ? { ok: false, why: 'that is a link to a file, not a link that carries the list itself' }%0A    : { ok: false, why: 'no list is carried in that text — a workspace link has a %23zdata=… (or %23data=…) part' };%0A}%0A%0A/** Decode whichever encoding the link used. Returns { text, encoding, bytes }.%0A    Throws a message meant for the user, because the usual failure here is a link%0A    that a chat client truncated, and "the list is incomplete" is the thing they%0A    need to know. */%0A/** Verify the integrity token, when the link carries one. A link without one is%0A    still opened — a person typing `%23data=` by hand cannot compute a checksum, and%0A    refusing their link would be pedantry. A link *with* a token that disagrees is%0A    refused, because that is the silent-partial-list case. */%0Afunction checkInlineDigest(raw, text, rawBytes) {%0A  const claimed = String(raw.sum || '').trim();%0A  if (!claimed) return { verified: false };%0A  /* The documented contract (llms.txt, workspace-link.html) hashes the same bytes%0A     the link deflates. Those are the *raw* bytes here — but `TextDecoder` strips a%0A     leading UTF-8 BOM, so a generator that built its list from a BOM'd file (Excel%0A     writes one) hashed three bytes the decoder no longer sees, and a correct link%0A     was refused as tampered. Verify against the raw bytes first — the contract —%0A     and fall back to the decoded text, which is what every app-built link has%0A     carried and what a generator that digests the BOM-less text produces. */%0A  if (rawBytes && claimed === inlineDigest(rawBytes)) return { verified: true };%0A  const actual = inlineDigest(new TextEncoder().encode(text));%0A  if (claimed !== actual) {%0A    throw new Error('this link is not what was sent — it decoded to a different list, which is what a link cut short in transit looks like');%0A  }%0A  return { verified: true };%0A}%0A%0Aasync function decodeInlineList(raw) {%0A  const z = String(raw.zdata || '').trim();%0A  const plain = String(raw.data || '');%0A  if (!z && !plain) throw new Error('this link carries no list in it');%0A  if (z) {%0A    let bytes;%0A    try { bytes = base64UrlToBytes(z); }%0A    catch (e) { throw new Error('the compressed list in this link is not valid base64 — it was probably truncated when it was shared'); }%0A    const out = await inflateRawBytes(bytes);%0A    if (out.length > INLINE_MAX_BYTES) throw new Error(`this link carries ${Math.round(out.length / 1048576)} MB of list — too much for a URL`);%0A    /* `TextDecoder` strips a leading UTF-8 BOM by default — the right parse outcome%0A       (Excel writes BOMs, the sniffer handles the rest) — so the raw inflated bytes%0A       ride along for the digest check above, which verifies the contract (the bytes%0A       the link carries) before falling back to the decoded text. */%0A    const text = new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(out);%0A    const { verified } = checkInlineDigest(raw, text, out);%0A    return { text, encoding: 'zdata', bytes: out.length, verified };%0A  }%0A  const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(plain);%0A  if (bytes.length > INLINE_MAX_BYTES) throw new Error(`this link carries ${Math.round(bytes.length / 1048576)} MB of list — too much for a URL`);%0A  const { verified } = checkInlineDigest(raw, plain);%0A  return { text: plain, encoding: 'data', bytes: bytes.length, verified };%0A}%0A%0A/** Build a workspace link for a list whose bytes we already have. Compressed when%0A    compression actually helps and the browser can do it, plain text when it does%0A    not — on a ten-row list the deflate header costs more than it saves. Returns%0A    { url, encoding, bytes, warning }. */%0Aasync function buildInlineLink(text, opts = {}) {%0A  const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(text);%0A  if (bytes.length > INLINE_MAX_BYTES) throw new Error(`that list is ${Math.round(bytes.length / 1048576)} MB — too big to carry in a URL`);%0A  let encoding = 'data', payload = encodeURIComponent(text);%0A  if (typeof CompressionStream === 'function') {%0A    const deflated = await deflateRawBytes(bytes);%0A    const candidate = bytesToBase64Url(deflated);%0A    /* Only when it is genuinely shorter: for a short list the base64 of a deflate%0A       stream is longer than the text itself, and `%23data=` is also readable. */%0A    if (candidate.length < payload.length * 0.9) { encoding = 'zdata'; payload = candidate; }%0A  }%0A  const base = opts.base || `'https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/app.html'`;%0A  const params = Object.assign({ sum: inlineDigest(bytes) }, opts.params || {});%0A  const extra = new URLSearchParams(params).toString();%0A  const url = `${base}%23${encoding}=${payload}${extra ? `&${extra}` : ''}`;%0A  const warning = bytes.length > INLINE_WARN_BYTES%0A    ? `That list is ${Math.round(bytes.length / 1024)} KB — some chat apps and mail clients trim links this long.`%0A    : '';%0A  log(`Workspace link built: ${encoding}, ${bytes.length} bytes of list → ${payload.length} chars of URL`);%0A  return { url, encoding, bytes: bytes.length, warning };%0A}%0A%0A/** Detect + parse any supported buffer into a matrix. Throws a friendly error for the rest. */%0Aasync function parseDetected(buf, det, sheetPick, htmlOpts) {%0A  const format = det.format;%0A  if (format === 'pdf') {%0A    throw new Error('PDF is not supported yet — export the list to CSV/XLSX first');%0A  }%0A  if (format === 'doc') {%0A    throw new Error('Legacy .doc (Word 97-2003) is not supported — open it in Word and save as .docx, or export the list as CSV');%0A  }%0A  if (format === 'docx') {%0A    // Word is read through the browser's own ZIP reader, so a build without it%0A    // must refuse out loud rather than fail on the first drop.%0A    if (!HAS_ZIP) throw new Error('this browser cannot unpack DOCX (no ZIP or XML support) — save the list as CSV or XLSX instead');%0A    return { rows: await parseDocx(buf), sheetName: null, format };%0A  }%0A  if (format === 'eml') {%0A    const { rows, from } = await parseEmlText(bytesToBinary(buf), { sheetPick });%0A    log(`Email import: ${rows.length} row(s) taken from the ${from}`);%0A    return { rows, sheetName: null, format, from };%0A  }%0A  if (isWorkbookFormat(format)) {%0A    if (!HAS_XLSX) throw new Error(`${formatLabel(format)} needs workbook support, which this build does not include — load a CSV, TSV, JSON, HTML or XML list instead`);%0A    const { rows, sheetName } = await parseWorkbook(buf, sheetPick);%0A    return { rows, sheetName, format };%0A  }%0A  const text = new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(buf);%0A  const rows = format === 'json' ? parseJsonText(text)%0A    : format === 'md' ? parseMarkdownText(text)%0A    : format === 'html' ? parseHtmlText(text, htmlOpts)%0A    : format === 'xml' ? parseXmlText(text)%0A    : parseDelimitedText(text, format);%0A  return { rows, sheetName: null, format };%0A}%0A%0A/** Pick a header column: an exact word ("Completed") outranks a prefix match%0A    ("Completed on", "Notes / comments"). Returns -1 when nothing matches. */%0Afunction pickColumn(header, exactWords, re) {%0A  const exact = header.findIndex(h => exactWords.has(normalizeHeader(h)));%0A  return exact >= 0 ? exact : header.findIndex(h => re.test(h));%0A}%0A%0A/** Detect header row + column roles from a 2D matrix. */%0Afunction analyzeMatrix(data) {%0A  // Trim fully-empty trailing rows%0A  while (data.length && data[data.length - 1].every(c => !String(c).trim())) data.pop();%0A%0A  const width = data.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 1);%0A  const first = (data[0] || []).map(c => String(c).trim());%0A%0A  // Header heuristic: known header words, or a first row with no URL values while later rows have URLs.%0A  const firstRowHasLink = first.some(c => linkKindOf(c));%0A  const sample = data.slice(1, 51);%0A  /* The old second clause needed a link below the first row to call it a header —%0A     which a *portal* list can never supply, because nothing in it is a link. So a%0A     first row that reads entirely like labels, over rows that do not, counts too.%0A     Guarded by "no link in the first row" either way, so a headerless list of%0A     values is still left headerless. */%0A  const hasHeader = first.some(c => HEADER_NAME_RE.test(c) || HEADER_URL_RE.test(c) || HEADER_STATUS_RE.test(c) || HEADER_NOTES_RE.test(c))%0A    || (!firstRowHasLink && (sample.some(r => r.some(c => linkKindOf(c))) || looksLikeLabelRow(first, sample)));%0A%0A  const header = hasHeader ? first : [];%0A  let urlCol = -1, nameCol = -1, statusCol = -1, notesCol = -1;%0A%0A  if (hasHeader) {%0A    header.forEach((h, i) => { if (nameCol < 0 && HEADER_NAME_RE.test(h)) nameCol = i; });%0A    statusCol = pickColumn(header, STATUS_HEADER_WORDS, HEADER_STATUS_RE);%0A    notesCol = pickColumn(header, NOTES_HEADER_WORDS, HEADER_NOTES_RE);%0A  }%0A%0A  /* URL column: score link-shaped *values* per column and take the winner. A%0A     URL, an email address and a phone number all count — weighted, so a list%0A     with both a Website and an Email column leads with the website while a list%0A     that only holds addresses still gets a working link column. Status/notes%0A     columns are skipped so a notes column full of pasted links never outbids the%0A     real one; the header name only settles an exact tie. */%0A  const skip = new Set([statusCol, notesCol].filter(c => c >= 0));%0A  const bodyStart = hasHeader ? 1 : 0;%0A  const sampleEnd = Math.min(data.length, bodyStart + 200);%0A  let bestCount = 0, bestHeaderMatch = false;%0A  for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) {%0A    if (skip.has(c)) continue;%0A    let n = 0;%0A    for (let r = bodyStart; r < sampleEnd; r++) n += LINK_WEIGHT[linkKindOf(data[r][c])] || 0;%0A    if (!n) continue;%0A    const headerMatch = hasHeader && HEADER_URL_RE.test(header[c] || '');%0A    if (n > bestCount || (n === bestCount && headerMatch && !bestHeaderMatch)) {%0A      bestCount = n; bestHeaderMatch = headerMatch; urlCol = c;%0A    }%0A  }%0A  if (urlCol < 0 && hasHeader) {%0A    const h = header.findIndex(x => HEADER_URL_RE.test(x));   // nothing link-shaped: trust the label%0A    if (h >= 0) urlCol = h;%0A  }%0A  if (urlCol < 0) {%0A    for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) if (c !== nameCol && !skip.has(c)) { urlCol = c; break; }%0A  }%0A  if (urlCol < 0) urlCol = 0;%0A%0A  /* Name column: a title-ish header decides, and an identifier column is never%0A     allowed to — `Ticket, Summary, …` must title its cards with the summary, not%0A     with `INC0041821`. Failing that, the first column with text that is neither%0A     the link, the status, the notes, nor an identifier. */%0A  if (nameCol < 0 && hasHeader) {%0A    nameCol = header.findIndex(h => HEADER_NAME_RE.test(String(h || '')) && !HEADER_ID_RE.test(String(h || '').trim()));%0A    if (nameCol >= 0) log(`Name column taken from the "${String(header[nameCol]).trim()}" header`);%0A  }%0A  const idish = hasHeader ? header.map(h => HEADER_ID_RE.test(String(h || '').trim())) : [];%0A  const firstTextColumn = (allowId) => {%0A    for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) {%0A      if (c === urlCol || skip.has(c)) continue;%0A      if (!allowId && idish[c]) continue;%0A      if (data.some(r => String(r[c] || '').trim())) return c;%0A    }%0A    return -1;%0A  };%0A  if (nameCol < 0) nameCol = firstTextColumn(false);%0A  if (nameCol < 0) nameCol = firstTextColumn(true);   // every column looked like an identifier%0A  log(`Matrix analyzed: header=${hasHeader}, urlCol=${urlCol} (${bestCount} link point${bestCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}${bestHeaderMatch ? ', header agreed' : ''}), nameCol=${nameCol}, statusCol=${statusCol}, notesCol=${notesCol}, width=${width}`);%0A  /* `linkless` is the signal that this is a *portal* list: not one cell anywhere%0A     looks like an address. That is not a broken list, it is a list whose rows are%0A     keys — so it gets a URL template instead of a link column. */%0A  return { hasHeader, urlCol, nameCol, statusCol, notesCol, width, linkless: bestCount === 0 };%0A}%0A%0A/** Load a normalized 2D matrix into app state. */%0Afunction loadMatrix(data, meta) {%0A  log(`loadMatrix: ${data.length} rows from "${meta.name}" (mode=${meta.mode}, ext=${meta.ext})`);%0A  const a = analyzeMatrix(data);%0A  // A column the user flagged in Settings outranks detection — and it must land%0A  // before the status/notes seeding below, so a re-flagged status column still%0A  // round-trips the file's progress.%0A  const roleRec = a.hasHeader ? loadRoles()[headerSignature(data[0] || [])] : null;%0A  if (applyRoleRecord(a, roleRec, a.width)) log(`Remembered column flags applied: URL=${a.urlCol}, name=${a.nameCol}, status=${a.statusCol}, notes=${a.notesCol}`);%0A  /* The editors are remembered the same way and read in the same place: this is the%0A     live store, and a preset may only fill the gap when there is no record here. */%0A  applyFieldRecord(a.hasHeader ? loadFields()[headerSignature(data[0] || [])] : null, a.width);%0A  const bodyRows = data.length - (a.hasHeader ? 1 : 0);%0A%0A  state.name = meta.name;%0A  state.ext = meta.ext;%0A  state.mode = meta.mode;%0A  state.fileHandle = meta.handle || null;%0A  state.sourceUrl = meta.sourceUrl || null;%0A  state.sheetName = meta.sheetName || 'Sheet1';%0A  state.data = data;%0A  state.hasHeader = a.hasHeader;%0A  state.urlCol = a.urlCol; state.nameCol = a.nameCol; state.statusCol = a.statusCol; state.notesCol = a.notesCol;%0A  state.linkless = a.linkless;%0A  /* Where a row's link comes from, decided once per file: an explicit `?link=`%0A     or the settings panel, else whatever was remembered for this header, else%0A     nothing (and the row's own link cell, if it has one). */%0A  const tplKey = templateKeyFor(data, a.hasHeader);%0A  const fromParam = String(meta.linkTemplate ?? bootLinkTemplate ?? '').trim();%0A  bootLinkTemplate = '';                       // one load only%0A  /* `?? ''` on the *remembered* value too, not just the incoming one: a header that%0A     has never carried a template has no entry, so this is `undefined` on every%0A     ordinary file — and `String(undefined)` is the string "undefined", which the%0A     URL builder would then happily turn into https://undefined for every row. */%0A  const remembered = String((tplKey ? loadTemplates()[tplKey] : '') ?? '').trim();%0A  state.linkTemplate = fromParam || remembered;%0A  if (fromParam && tplKey) rememberTemplate(tplKey, fromParam);%0A  if (state.linkTemplate) log(`Link template for this list: ${state.linkTemplate}`);%0A%0A  // Seed per-card status/notes. Priority: explicit session restore > the file's%0A  // own Status/Notes columns (round-trip) > blank state.%0A  const n = bodyRows;%0A  const fileHasCols = a.hasHeader && (a.statusCol >= 0 || a.notesCol >= 0);%0A  const headerRow = data[0] || [];%0A  const statusName = a.statusCol >= 0 ? String(headerRow[a.statusCol] || 'Status') : 'Status';%0A  const notesName  = a.notesCol  >= 0 ? String(headerRow[a.notesCol]  || 'Notes')  : 'Notes';%0A  const seeded = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => {%0A    const row = data[i + (a.hasHeader ? 1 : 0)] || [];%0A    const raw = a.statusCol >= 0 ? String(row[a.statusCol] || '').trim() : '';%0A    return isCompleteValue(raw) ? 'complete' : 'incomplete';%0A  });%0A  const seededNotes = a.hasHeader && a.notesCol >= 0%0A    ? Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => String((data[i + (a.hasHeader ? 1 : 0)] || [])[a.notesCol] ?? ''))%0A    : null;%0A  const restoring = Array.isArray(meta.status) && meta.status.length === n;%0A  state.status = restoring ? meta.status.slice() : seeded;%0A  state.notes  = restoring ? (Array.isArray(meta.notes) && meta.notes.length === n ? meta.notes.slice() : Array(n).fill(''))%0A               : (seededNotes || Array(n).fill(''));%0A%0A  // Round-trip resume: an exported/updated file dropped back in carries the%0A  // user's progress in its completed status + notes columns. Report what was%0A  // picked up so "continue where you left off" is visible, not silent.%0A  const seededDone = seeded.filter(s => s === 'complete').length;%0A  const seededWithNotes = seededNotes ? seededNotes.filter(s => String(s).trim()).length : 0;%0A  const resumed = [];%0A  if (!restoring && fileHasCols) {%0A    if (a.statusCol >= 0) {%0A      log(`Seeded ${seededDone} 'complete' status(es) from the file's ${statusName} column (round-trip)`);%0A      if (seededDone) resumed.push(`${seededDone} complete`);%0A    }%0A    if (a.notesCol >= 0) {%0A      log(`Seeded ${seededWithNotes} note(s) from the file's ${notesName} column (round-trip)`);%0A      if (seededWithNotes) resumed.push(`${seededWithNotes} note${seededWithNotes === 1 ? '' : 's'}`);%0A    }%0A  }%0A%0A  state.isDirty = false;%0A  closeAllTabs();%0A  els.search.value = ''; state.search = '';%0A  els.showCompleted.checked = false; state.hideCompleted = true;  // completed hidden by default%0A  state.sortCol = null; state.sortAsc = true; els.sortDir.textContent = '↓';%0A  state.expanded = {};%0A  applyLayoutFor(state.data[0] || []);   // auto-apply a saved preset when the header matches%0A  buildSortOptions();%0A%0A  updateChrome();%0A  renderCards();%0A  els.welcome.hidden = true;   // %23welcome[hidden] in the stylesheet — no inline write needed%0A  maybeShowFirstRunPicker();%0A  maybeOfferPortalSetup();%0A  const noun = `task${n === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;%0A  toast(`Loaded ${n} ${noun} from ${state.name}${resumed.length ? ` — resumed ${resumed.join(' · ')}` : ''}`, 'success');%0A}%0A%0A/* ----------------------- First-run open-mode picker ----------------------- */%0Aconst LS_SEEN_PICKER = 'turnstone-mode-picked';%0A%0Afunction maybeShowFirstRunPicker() {%0A  let seen = false;%0A  try { seen = localStorage.getItem(LS_SEEN_PICKER) === '1'; } catch (e) {}%0A  if (seen) return;%0A  showModePicker(true);%0A}%0A%0A/** Ask the user how links should open (first run, or later via the menu). */%0Afunction showModePicker(firstRun) {%0A  log(`Showing open-mode picker (firstRun=${firstRun})`);%0A  const overlay = document.createElement('div');%0A  overlay.id = 'mode-picker';%0A  const opts = Object.entries(OPEN_MODES).map(([k, v]) => `%0A    <button data-pick="${k}" class="pick-opt">%0A      <span class="label">${v.label}</span>%0A      <span class="hint">${v.hint}</span>%0A    </button>`).join('');%0A  overlay.innerHTML = `%0A    <div class="modal-box">%0A      <h3 class="modal-title">How do you want to work through your links?</h3>%0A      <p class="modal-sub">You can change this anytime from the ☰ menu.</p>%0A      ${opts}%0A      <button id="picker-later" class="modal-cancel">${firstRun ? 'Decide later (tabs by default)' : 'Cancel'}</button>%0A    </div>`;%0A  mountPoint().appendChild(overlay);%0A  const done = () => { overlay.remove(); };%0A  overlay.querySelectorAll('button[data-pick]').forEach(b => {%0A    b.onclick = () => {%0A      setOpenMode(b.dataset.pick, false);%0A      try { localStorage.setItem(LS_SEEN_PICKER, '1'); } catch (e) {}%0A      toast(`Links will open as ${OPEN_MODES[b.dataset.pick].label.toLowerCase()}`, 'success');%0A      done();%0A    };%0A  });%0A  overlay.querySelector('%23picker-later').onclick = () => {%0A    try { localStorage.setItem(LS_SEEN_PICKER, '1'); } catch (e) {}%0A    log('Open-mode picker deferred — staying with current mode');%0A    done();%0A  };%0A}%0A%0A/* ------------------------- Card column layout ----------------------------- */%0Aconst COLLAPSED_COLS = 3;   // data columns shown on a collapsed card%0Aconst LS_PRESETS = 'turnstone-col-presets';%0A%0A/** Header signature: trimmed, lowercased header values joined with '¦'. */%0Afunction headerSignature(headerRow) {%0A  return (headerRow || []).map(h => String(h || '').trim().toLowerCase()).join('¦');%0A}%0A%0Afunction loadPresets() {%0A  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_PRESETS) || '{}'); }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not read column presets', e); return {}; }%0A}%0A%0Afunction savePresets(p) {%0A  try { localStorage.setItem(LS_PRESETS, JSON.stringify(p)); return true; }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not persist column presets', e); return false; }%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Column roles: which column is the URL / name / status / notes ---- */%0A/* Detection reads values and is right most of the time; when it is not, the%0A   settings panel lets the user say so. That flag is remembered per header%0A   signature, so re-opening the same list — or the same export — keeps it. */%0Aconst LS_ROLES = 'turnstone-col-roles';%0Aconst ROLE_FIELDS = { url: 'urlCol', name: 'nameCol', status: 'statusCol', notes: 'notesCol' };%0Aconst ROLE_LABELS = { '': 'Data column', url: 'URL', name: 'Name', status: 'Status', notes: 'Notes' };%0A%0Afunction loadRoles() {%0A  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_ROLES) || '{}'); }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not read column flags', e); return {}; }%0A}%0Afunction saveRoles(r) {%0A  try { localStorage.setItem(LS_ROLES, JSON.stringify(r)); return true; }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not persist column flags', e); return false; }%0A}%0A%0A/** Which role a column currently holds ('' when it is an ordinary data column). */%0Afunction columnRole(c) {%0A  for (const [role, field] of Object.entries(ROLE_FIELDS)) if (state[field] === c) return role;%0A  return '';%0A}%0A%0A/** Remember this header shape's role assignment. Headerless lists have no stable%0A    signature, so their flags last for the session only. */%0Afunction persistRoles() {%0A  if (!state.hasHeader) { log('No header row to key column flags to — flags last this session only'); return; }%0A  const sig = headerSignature(state.data[0]);%0A  const all = loadRoles();%0A  all[sig] = { url: state.urlCol, name: state.nameCol, status: state.statusCol, notes: state.notesCol, ts: Date.now() };%0A  if (saveRoles(all)) log(`Column flags saved for header signature: URL=${state.urlCol}, name=${state.nameCol}, status=${state.statusCol}, notes=${state.notesCol}`);%0A}%0A%0A/** Overlay a remembered role record onto a role set (analysis `a` or `state`).%0A    Detection proposes; a recorded flag decides — out-of-range values are ignored%0A    so schema drift degrades to detection instead of a broken column. */%0Afunction applyRoleRecord(target, rec, width) {%0A  if (!rec || typeof rec !== 'object') return false;%0A  const ok = (v) => Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0 && v < width;%0A  const set = (field, v) => {%0A    if (v === -1) { if (field !== 'urlCol') target[field] = -1; }   // URL must always land somewhere%0A    else if (ok(v)) target[field] = v;%0A  };%0A  set('urlCol', rec.url); set('nameCol', rec.name); set('statusCol', rec.status); set('notesCol', rec.notes);%0A  return true;%0A}%0A%0A/** Assign a role to a column from the settings panel ('' clears it back to data). */%0Afunction setColumnRole(col, role) {%0A  const prev = columnRole(col);%0A  if (prev) state[ROLE_FIELDS[prev]] = -1;%0A  if (role && ROLE_FIELDS[role]) {%0A    const holder = state[ROLE_FIELDS[role]];%0A    if (holder >= 0 && holder !== col) log(`Column ${holder} (${colLabel(holder)}) released the ${role} role → data column`);%0A    state[ROLE_FIELDS[role]] = col;%0A    delete state.colHidden[col];   // a role column is a card feature, never hidden%0A  }%0A  log(`Column ${col} (${colLabel(col)}) flagged as ${ROLE_LABELS[role] || 'Data column'}`);%0A  persistRoles();%0A  renderCards();%0A  renderSettings();%0A}%0A%0A/* ---- Column field types: how a cell is *edited* on a card ------------------ */%0A/* Three different questions get asked about a column and they are answered in%0A   three different places on purpose:%0A%0A     · what is it?       — the role (URL / name / status / notes), which the card%0A                           layout itself is built around;%0A     · where does it go? — the order and the hidden set, which are display only; and%0A     · how is it edited? — this: read-only by default, because most columns are%0A                           somebody else's data that the queue only has to show,%0A                           but a column you keep updating (a stage, an owner, a next%0A                           action, a date) deserves a real control.%0A%0A   Read-only stays the default deliberately: turning every cell of every column into%0A   a field would make a queue you are only reading look like one you are expected to%0A   maintain, and the app's claim is that it shows you the list you already have. */%0Aconst LS_FIELDS = 'turnstone-col-fields';%0Aconst FIELD_TYPES = { '': 'Read only', text: 'Text', long: 'Long text', select: 'Dropdown', buttons: 'Buttons' };%0Aconst CHOICE_TYPES = new Set(['select', 'buttons']);%0Aconst MAX_SEEDED_OPTIONS = 24;   // a column with 200 distinct values is not a dropdown%0A%0Afunction loadFields() {%0A  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_FIELDS) || '{}'); }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not read column editors', e); return {}; }%0A}%0Afunction saveFields(f) {%0A  try { localStorage.setItem(LS_FIELDS, JSON.stringify(f)); return true; }%0A  catch (e) { warn('Could not persist column editors', e); return false; }%0A}%0A%0A/** Persist this file's editor types and choice lists, keyed exactly like roles and%0A    presets. An entry is removed when nothing is set, so a file that has been reset%0A    does not leave an empty record behind that makes the next load look edited.%0A    A headerless list has no stable signature, so its editors last the session. */%0Afunction persistFields() {%0A  if (!state.hasHeader) { log('No header row to key column editors to — they last this session only'); return; }%0A  const sig = headerSignature(state.data[0]);%0A  const all = loadFields();%0A  const rec = { types: {}, options: {}, ts: Date.now() };%0A  for (const [c, t] of Object.entries(state.colTypes)) if (t && FIELD_TYPES[t]) rec.types[c] = t;%0A  for (const [c, list] of Object.entries(state.colOptions)) if (Array.isArray(list) && list.length) rec.options[c] = list;%0A  if (Object.keys(rec.types).length || Object.keys(rec.options).length) all[sig] = rec;%0A  else delete all[sig];%0A  if (saveFields(all)) log(`Column editors saved: ${Object.keys(rec.types).length} typed column(s), ${Object.keys(rec.options).length} with choices`);%0A}%0A%0A/** Overlay a remembered editor record onto the live state (null clears it). */%0Afunction applyFieldRecord(rec, width) {%0A  state.colTypes = {};%0A  state.colOptions = {};%0A  if (!rec || typeof rec !== 'object') return false;%0A  const ok = (c) => Number.isInteger(c) && c >= 0 && c < width;%0A  for (const [c, t] of Object.entries(rec.types || {})) if (ok(+c) && FIELD_TYPES[t]) state.colTypes[+c] = t;%0A  for (const [c, list] of Object.entries(rec.options || {})) if (ok(+c) && Array.isArray(list)) state.colOptions[+c] = list.map(String).slice(0, 40);%0A  const typed = Object.keys(state.colTypes).length;%0A  if (typed || Object.keys(state.colOptions).length) log(`Column editors applied from storage: ${typed} typed column(s)`);%0A  return true;%0A}%0A%0A/** The values a column already holds, **most common first**. This is the seed for a%0A    choice list, so a dropdown offers the vocabulary the file actually uses — and the%0A    ordering is the point rather than a detail: a status column should open on the%0A    status that happens most, not on whichever value starts with “A”. */%0Afunction columnValues(c) {%0A  const counts = new Map();%0A  for (let i = 0; i < cardCount(); i++) {%0A    const v = String(((state.data[i + (state.hasHeader ? 1 : 0)] || [])[c] ?? '')).trim();%0A    if (v) counts.set(v, (counts.get(v) || 0) + 1);%0A  }%0A  return [...counts].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1] || a[0].localeCompare(b[0])).map(([v]) => v);%0A}%0A%0A/** Fill a column's choice list from its own values. Offered as a button because it%0A    is the difference between a dropdown you have to populate by hand and one that is%0A    useful the moment you pick the type. */%0Afunction seedOptions(c) {%0A  const all = columnValues(c);%0A  if (!all.length) { toast(`No values in “${colLabel(c)}” to build choices from`, 'error'); return; }%0A  const list = all.slice(0, MAX_SEEDED_OPTIONS);%0A  state.colOptions[c] = list;%0A  log(`Choices seeded for column ${c} from ${all.length} distinct value(s), ${list.length} kept`);%0A  toast(all.length > list.length%0A    ? `${list.length} choices taken from “${colLabel(c)}” — the rest are past the ${MAX_SEEDED_OPTIONS}-choice cap`%0A    : `${list.length} choice${list.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} taken from “${colLabel(c)}”`, 'success');%0A  persistFields();%0A  renderCards();%0A  renderSettings();%0A}%0A%0A/** Set a column's field type. Switching *to* a choice type with an empty list seeds%0A    it from the file, because a dropdown with no options is not an empty control —%0A    it is a broken one. */%0Afunction setFieldType(c, type) {%0A  if (!FIELD_TYPES[type]) type = '';%0A  if (columnRole(c)) { toast('That column is a card feature — Status and Notes have their own controls', 'error'); return; }%0A  const prev = state.colTypes[c] || '';%0A  if (!type) delete state.colTypes[c];%0A  else { state.colTypes[c] = type; delete state.colHidden[c]; }   // an editor on a hidden column is one nobody can reach%0A  log(`Column ${c} (${colLabel(c)}) editor: ${FIELD_TYPES[prev]} → ${FIELD_TYPES[type]}`);%0A  if (CHOICE_TYPES.has(type) && !fieldOptions(c).length) { seedOptions(c); return; }  // seeds, persists and re-renders%0A  persistFields();%0A  renderCards();%0A  renderSettings();%0A}%0A%0A/** The choices a dropdown or a button array offers. Read through this rather than%0A    touching the map, so the "not set" case is one answer everywhere. */%0Afunction fieldOptions(c) { return state.colOptions[c] || []; }%0A%0A/** Replace a column's choice list. `live` is true while the user is typing in the%0A    panel's field, where re-rendering the panel would take the caret with it — the%0A    cards still follow along on every keystroke. */%0Afunction setFieldOptions(c, value, live = false) {%0A  const seen = new Set();%0A  const list = String(value || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)%0A    .filter(v => (seen.has(v) ? false : seen.add(v))).slice(0, 40);%0A  state.colOptions[c] = list;%0A  persistFields();%0A  renderCards();%0A  if (live) log(`Choices for column ${c}: ${list.length}`);%0A  else { log(`Choices for column ${c} set to ${list.length}: ${list.join(' · ')}`); renderSettings(); }%0A}%0A%0A/** Move everything remembered about a list from one header signature to another.%0A%0A    All of it — the column flags, the editors, the preset and the portal template —%0A    is keyed by the header row, so renaming one column would orphan the lot in a%0A    single keystroke. The column *indices* are unaffected by a rename, which is why%0A    nothing inside these records has to be renumbered; only the key moves. */%0Afunction rekeySignature(oldSig, newSig) {%0A  if (!oldSig || !newSig || oldSig === newSig) return;%0A  const moves = [];%0A  const roles = loadRoles();%0A  if (roles[oldSig]) { roles[newSig] = roles[oldSig]; delete roles[oldSig]; saveRoles(roles); moves.push('column flags'); }%0A  const fields = loadFields();%0A  if (fields[oldSig]) { fields[newSig] = fields[oldSig]; delete fields[oldSig]; saveFields(fields); moves.push('column editors'); }%0A  const presets = loadPresets();%0A  if (presets[oldSig]) { presets[newSig] = presets[oldSig]; delete presets[oldSig]; savePresets(presets); moves.push('layout preset'); }%0A  const templates = loadTemplates();%0A  if (templates[oldSig]) { templates[newSig] = templates[oldSig]; delete templates[oldSig]; saveTemplates(templates); moves.push('portal template'); }%0A  try {%0A    const list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_PORTAL_DECLINED) || '[]') || [];%0A    if (list.includes(oldSig)) { localStorage.setItem(LS_PORTAL_DECLINED, JSON.stringify(list.map(k => k === oldSig ? newSig : k))); moves.push('declined prompt'); }%0A  } catch (e) { /* storage blocked */ }%0A  log(moves.length ? `Re-keyed after rename: ${moves.join(', ')}` : 'Renamed with nothing remembered to re-key');%0A}%0A%0A/** Rename a column — by editing its header cell, which is the rename people mean.%0A%0A    Not a display alias: the header row is what gets exported, what a portal%0A    template's `{Column}` names, and what the sort dropdown lists, so a second private%0A    name for the same column would be a worse lie than the original. The header cell%0A    changes, the signature changes with it, and everything keyed by that signature is%0A    carried over (`rekeySignature`) — including the template's own `{Old name}`%0A    placeholders, which would otherwise silently stop composing a link for every row. */%0Afunction renameColumn(c, name) {%0A  if (!state.hasHeader) { toast('This file has no header row to rename', 'error'); renderSettings(); return; }%0A  const header = state.data[0] || [];%0A  const before = String(header[c] ?? '').trim();%0A  const after = String(name ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 120);%0A  if (!after) { toast('A column needs a name', 'error'); renderSettings(); return; }%0A  if (after === before) return;%0A  const oldSig = headerSignature(state.data[0]);%0A  header[c] = after;%0A  const newSig = headerSignature(state.data[0]);%0A  rekeySignature(oldSig, newSig);%0A  if (state.linkTemplate && before) {%0A    const next = state.linkTemplate.split(`{${before}}`).join(`{${after}}`);%0A    if (next !== state.linkTemplate) {%0A      state.linkTemplate = next;%0A      rememberTemplate(newSig, next);%0A      log(`Portal template placeholder {${before}} → {${after}}`);%0A    }%0A  }%0A  log(`Column ${c} renamed: “${before}” → “${after}” (header signature changed)`);%0A  toast(`Renamed to “${after}” — the header cell changes in the file you export`, 'success');%0A  buildSortOptions();%0A  renderCards();%0A  renderSettings();%0A  markDirty();%0A}%0A%0A/** If a saved preset matches this file's header exactly, apply its layout. */%0Afunction applyLayoutFor(headerRow) {%0A  const width = (state.data[0] || []).length;%0A  if (!width) return;%0A  const sig = headerSignature(headerRow);%0A  const presets = loadPresets();%0A  const preset = sig && presets[sig];%0A  if (preset && Array.isArray(preset.colOrder)) {%0A    const valid = preset.colOrder.filter(c => Number.isInteger(c) && c >= 0 && c < width);%0A    for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) if (!valid.includes(c)) valid.push(c); // tolerate schema drift%0A    state.colOrder = valid;%0A    state.colHidden = {};%0A    for (const c of preset.hidden || []) if (c >= 0 && c < width) state.colHidden[c] = true;%0A    // The live flag store wins over a preset's copy: a preset is only saved on%0A    // demand, so it can be stale the moment the user re-flags a column.%0A    if (preset.roles && !loadRoles()[sig] && applyRoleRecord(state, preset.roles, width)) log('Preset also carried column flags (URL/name/status/notes)');%0A    if (preset.fields && !loadFields()[sig] && applyFieldRecord(preset.fields, width)) log('Preset also carried column editors (field types and choice lists)');%0A    log(`Preset "${preset.name}" auto-applied (header signature matched)`);%0A    toast(`Layout preset "${preset.name}" applied`, 'success');%0A  } else {%0A    state.colOrder = null;%0A    state.colHidden = {};%0A    log('No matching layout preset for this header — using file order');%0A  }%0A}%0A%0A/** Data-column display order for cards (fixed roles excluded). */%0Afunction cardColumns() {%0A  const width = state.data.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0);%0A  const fixed = new Set([state.urlCol, state.nameCol, state.statusCol, state.notesCol].filter(c => c >= 0));%0A  const all = [];%0A  for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) if (!fixed.has(c)) all.push(c);%0A  const order = state.colOrder ? state.colOrder.filter(c => !fixed.has(c) && c < width) : [];%0A  for (const c of all) if (!order.includes(c)) order.push(c); // append anything the preset didn't mention%0A  return order.filter(c => !state.colHidden[c]);%0A}%0A%0Afunction colLabel(c) {%0A  if (state.hasHeader) return String((state.data[0] || [])[c] || '').trim() || `Column ${c + 1}`;%0A  return `Column ${c + 1}`;%0A}%0A%0Afunction visibleCardCount() { return cardColumns().length; }%0A%0A/* ------------------------------ Settings UI -------------------------------- */%0Afunction openSettings() {%0A  log('Opening column settings');%0A  renderSettings();%0A  /* The portal field is mounted here rather than written into the markup, so it%0A     can list this file's own columns as chips and preview against a real row. */%0A  const input = document.getElementById('portal-set-input');%0A  if (input) input.value = state.linkTemplate;%0A  const refresh = wirePortalEditor('portal-set', { onCommit: null });%0A  const apply = document.getElementById('portal-set-apply');%0A  const clear = document.getElementById('portal-set-clear');%0A  if (apply) apply.onclick = () => { applyPortalTemplate(input.value); openSettings(); };%0A  if (clear) clear.onclick = () => { input.value = ''; applyPortalTemplate(''); openSettings(); };%0A  if (refresh) refresh();%0A  els.settingsOverlay.hidden = false;%0A}%0Afunction closeSettings() { els.settingsOverlay.hidden = true; }%0A%0Afunction renderSettings() {%0A  const width = state.data.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0);%0A  const order = state.colOrder ? state.colOrder.filter(c => c < width) : [];%0A  for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) if (!order.includes(c)) order.push(c);%0A%0A  /* Position numbers count the columns a card actually puts in that order. The role%0A     columns are pinned features (name, URL, status, notes) and are not in it, so%0A     numbering them 1–5 here said "%234" of a sequence the reader could only see two of. */%0A  const dataOrder = order.filter(c => !columnRole(c));%0A  const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();%0A  for (const c of order) {%0A    const role = columnRole(c);%0A    const type = state.colTypes[c] || '';%0A    const div = document.createElement('div');%0A    div.className = 'set-col' + (role ? ' fixed' : '') + (CHOICE_TYPES.has(type) ? ' has-choices' : '');%0A    div.draggable = !role;%0A    div.dataset.col = c;%0A    const name = esc(colLabel(c));%0A    const roleOpts = ['', 'url', 'name', 'status', 'notes']%0A      .map(r => `<option value="${r}"${r === role ? ' selected' : ''}>${ROLE_LABELS[r]}</option>`).join('');%0A    const typeOpts = Object.entries(FIELD_TYPES)%0A      .map(([v, label]) => `<option value="${v}"${v === type ? ' selected' : ''}>${label}</option>`).join('');%0A    div.innerHTML =%0A      `<span class="drag"${role ? '' : ' title="Drag to reorder"'}>⋮⋮</span>%0A       ${role ? '' : `<input type="checkbox" data-colshow="${c}" aria-label="Show ${name} on cards" title="Show on cards" ${state.colHidden[c] ? '' : 'checked'}>`}%0A       <input class="cname" type="text" data-colname="${c}" value="${name}"${state.hasHeader ? '' : ' disabled'}%0A              title="${state.hasHeader ? return; }%0A  const name = els.presetName.value.trim();%0A  if (!name) { toast('Give the preset a name first', 'error'); return; }%0A  const width = state.data.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0);%0A  const order = state.colOrder ? state.colOrder.filter(c => c < width) : [];%0A  for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) if (!order.includes(c)) order.push(c);%0A  const hidden = Object.keys(state.colHidden).map(Number).filter(c => c < width);%0A  const sig = headerSignature(state.data[0]);%0A  const roles = { url: state.urlCol, name: state.nameCol, status: state.statusCol, notes: state.notesCol };%0A  /* The editors ride along in the preset, so a layout that includes them is restored%0A     whole — a preset that remembered the order but not which columns were editable%0A     would be a layout with a hole in it. */%0A  const fields = { types: { ...state.colTypes }, options: { ...state.colOptions } };%0A  const presets = loadPresets();%0A  presets[sig] = { name, colOrder: order, hidden, roles, fields, ts: Date.now() };%0A  if (savePresets(presets)) {%0A    log(`Column preset "${name}" saved for header signature (${sig.split('¦').length} cols)`);%0A    toast(`Preset "${name}" saved — files with this exact header auto-apply it`, 'success');%0A    els.presetName.value = '';%0A    renderSettings();%0A  } else toast('Could not save preset (storage unavailable?)', 'error');%0A}%0A%0Afunction applyPresetByKey(sig) {%0A  const p = loadPresets()[sig];%0A  if (!p) return;%0A  const width = state.data.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0);%0A  state.colOrder = (p.colOrder || []).slice();%0A  state.colHidden = {};%0A  for (const c of p.hidden || []) state.colHidden[c] = true;%0A  state.expanded = {};%0A  if (p.roles && applyRoleRecord(state, p.roles, width)) {%0A    log('Preset carried column flags (URL/name/status/notes) — remembering them for this header');%0A    persistRoles();   // the live store follows an explicit preset apply%0A  }%0A  /* Editors come from the preset *as a whole*, including the case where it has none:%0A     applying a saved layout should put the columns back the way they were when it was%0A     saved, not merge with whatever happens to be set now. */%0A  applyFieldRecord(p.fields || null, width);%0A  persistFields();%0A  log(`Preset "${p.name}" applied manually`);%0A  renderCards();%0A  renderSettings();%0A}%0A%0A/** Back to the file's own arrangement: no reordering, nothing hidden, no editors.%0A    The stored record is deleted rather than merely forgotten, so re-opening the file%0A    cannot resurrect a layout the user has cleared. */%0Afunction resetColLayout() {%0A  state.colOrder = null;%0A  state.colHidden = {};%0A  state.colTypes = {};%0A  state.colOptions = {};%0A  state.expanded = {};%0A  persistFields();%0A  log('Column layout reset to file order (order, visibility and editors cleared)');%0A  renderCards();%0A  renderSettings();%0A}%0A%0A/* ---------------------- Portal lists (no links at all) -------------------- */%0A/* The editor is one control mounted twice: the prompt offered when a list turns%0A   out to have no link-shaped value anywhere, and the same field in the settings%0A   panel for changing your mind later. `ns` namespaces the field ids so both can%0A   be in the DOM at once. */%0Aconst LS_PORTAL_DECLINED = 'turnstone-portal-declined';%0A%0A/** The columns a template may name — header names, or positions when there is no%0A    header row to name. */%0Afunction templateColumns() {%0A  return templateColumnsFor(state.data, state.hasHeader);%0A}%0A%0A/** The same naming rule for any matrix, not just the loaded one — the share-link%0A    builder previews a list that is not loaded yet, and its chips must name columns%0A    exactly as the live editor would name them. */%0Afunction templateColumnsFor(rows, hasHeader) {%0A  const data = rows || [];%0A  const header = hasHeader ? (data[0] || []) : [];%0A  const width = data.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.length), 0);%0A  const out = [];%0A  for (let c = 0; c < width; c++) {%0A    const name = String(header[c] ?? '').trim();%0A    out.push(name ? { label: name, field: name } : { label: `column ${c + 1}`, field: String(c) });%0A  }%0A  return out;%0A}%0A%0A/** The row a preview should be built from: the first row that looks like data. */%0Afunction firstBodyRow() {%0A  return state.data[state.hasHeader ? 1 : 0] || state.data[0] || [];%0A}%0A%0A/** Wire the input, the column chips and the live preview for one editor. Calls%0A    `onCommit(value)` on every keystroke, so the cards follow along as you type. */%0Afunction wirePortalEditor(ns, { onCommit } = {}) {%0A  const input = document.getElementById(`${ns}-input`);%0A  const chips = document.getElementById(`${ns}-chips`);%0A  const preview = document.getElementById(`${ns}-preview`);%0A  if (!input || !chips || !preview) return;%0A  chips.innerHTML = '';%0A  for (const col of templateColumns()) {%0A    const b = document.createElement('button');%0A    b.className = 'pchip';%0A    b.type = 'button';%0A    b.textContent = `{${col.label}}`;%0A    b.title = `Insert {${col.field}}`;%0A    b.onclick = () => {%0A      const at = input.selectionStart ?? input.value.length;%0A      input.value = input.value.slice(0, at) + `{${col.field}}` + input.value.slice(input.selectionEnd ?? at);%0A      input.focus();%0A      input.selectionStart = input.selectionEnd = at + col.field.length + 2;%0A      refresh();%0A    };%0A    chips.appendChild(b);%0A  }%0A  const refresh = () => {%0A    const value = input.value.trim();%0A    const problem = templateProblem(value, state.hasHeader ? (state.data[0] || []) : []);%0A    const composed = value ? applyUrlTemplate(value, firstBodyRow(), state.hasHeader ? (state.data[0] || []) : []) : '';%0A    input.classList.toggle('bad', !!problem);%0A    preview.className = 'portal-preview' + (problem ? ${templateFields(state.linkTemplate).length} per-row field(s)`);%0A    toast(`Links are now built from your rows — ${host}`, 'success');%0A  } else log('Portal template cleared — back to the file\'s own link column');%0A  markDirty();%0A  renderCards();%0A}%0A%0Afunction portalDeclined(key) {%0A  try { return (JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_PORTAL_DECLINED) || '[]') || []).includes(key); }%0A  catch (e) { return false; }%0A}%0Afunction declinePortal(key) {%0A  if (!key) return;%0A  try {%0A    const list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS_PORTAL_DECLINED) || '[]') || [];%0A    if (!list.includes(key)) list.push(key);%0A    localStorage.setItem(LS_PORTAL_DECLINED, JSON.stringify(list));%0A  } catch (e) { warn('Could not remember that you declined the portal prompt', e); }%0A}%0A%0A/** Offer the portal prompt once, for a list that has no links anywhere. */%0Afunction maybeOfferPortalSetup() {%0A  if (!state.linkless || state.linkTemplate || !cardCount()) return;%0A  if (modalOpen('%23mode-picker, %23menu')) { log('Portal prompt deferred — another modal is open'); With nothing loaded the placeholder does the teaching. */%0A  const prefilled = cardCount() > 0%0A    ? Papa.unparse(buildExportMatrix(), { delimiter: state.ext === 'tsv' ? '\t' : ',' })%0A    : '';%0A  const overlay = document.createElement('div');%0A  overlay.id = 'build-modal';%0A  overlay.innerHTML = `%0A    <div class="modal-box">%0A      <h3 placeholder="Name,URL,Status,Notes&%2310;Apple Newsroom,https://www.apple.com/newsroom/,incomplete,Q3 earnings&%2310;BBC Homepage,https://www.bbc.com/,complete,"></textarea>%0A      <p <label class="bl-label" for="bl-name">Name this workspace (optional)</label>%0A      <input type="text" id="bl-name" class="portal-input" spellcheck="false" autocomplete="off" placeholder="Q3      <div class="srow">%0A        <button class="btn primary" id="bl-copy">Copy link</button>%0A        <button class="btn" id="bl-open">Open it here</button>%0A        <button class="modal-cancel"
